Initial metadata identity checks use SHOW FRONTENDS/SHOW TABLETS, requiring a dedicated Doris ADMIN account; a least-privilege alternative is unfinished. Console roles are separate. Business readers should access views only. SQL/HTTP TLS still requires acceptance. Default three replicas requires enough BEs. One-BE tests must explicitly select replicas: 1 ; the service never silently lowers redundancy. Replicas range 1–5; buckets default 4, range 1–64. Compose resource limits describe fixtures, not throughput standards. The Web wizard exposes SQL/HTTP origins, redirect allowlist, replicas, buckets and index policy. Check before starting. Check reads source definitions and probes SQL features/HTTP health; it creates no tables and does not establish LOAD/DDL privileges. SQL enforces finite connect/socket timeouts and disables Connector/J cancellation timers to avoid their disconnect-cleanup null pointer. Arbitrary programming errors are not reclassified as networking. HTTP has independent connect/read/request/response bounds and never silently retries an ambiguous PUT internally. Confirmation and failures Loads require strict mode, zero filtering and exact input-row confirmation. Publish Timeout/running labels do not advance checkpoints. Each attempt uses a new load label: versioned rows/permanent destination receipts provide idempotency, not cancelled/expired labels. Success/finished labels still require native row key/version/tombstone/value verification; metadata content is also read back. After confirming data, the service persists a target batch receipt, then Journal transport progress, then the subscription checkpoint. Ambiguous responses/crashes can replay. Destinations acknowledge independently: relational targets can progress through a Doris outage until journal quota imposes backpressure. Restart checks native tablet identity, ownership, DDL, views and latest confirmed receipt. Initialized missing objects are not recreated empty at an old checkpoint. Restoring a coherent older nonempty FE+BE backup while keeping a newer journal is refused when the newest receipt is absent. Restore the right target or plan a rebuild. Coordinate data, metadata and journal backups; arbitrary per-table/incoherent rollback or external tampering requires reconciliation and is not comprehensively detected. Pause reports UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT MATERIALIZATION ; already submitted requests cannot be retracted. Relational targets may report FENCED. This is not a Doris business cutover barrier. Deterministic data/schema/permission faults pause that subscription; after repair resume its error generation without skipping the original transaction. FAQ Where are business UNIQUE/GSI constraints? They become nonunique acceleration. Source enforcement and exclusive synchronization preserve caught-up data; external writes are unsupported. Doris internal UNIQUE KEY protects row identity, not business uniqueness. Why views and private tables? They hide occurrence IDs, versions and tombstones while preserving public column order. Do not replace views with unrelated tables or treat private storage as identical source DDL. SQL connects but loading fails? HTTP health does not test LOAD privilege, and SQL/HTTP are separate entries. Verify same-cluster origins, accounts, privileges and explicit FE redirect destinations. Does one SQL fault stop all targets? Deterministic faults pause their target. Repair and use independent UI resume or resume config.yml subscriptionId expectedErrorGeneration ; do not edit GTIDs/checkpoints. Can it adopt existing nonempty objects? Current ownership checks create missing private objects/views and reject conflicting existing data/layout. Adoption, live DDL, layout migration and cutover workflows remain unfinished. Does retained space clean itself? Source journals reclaim by independent ACK. Target receipts/tombstones/indexes are outside logical journal quota and need storage monitoring. Receipt compaction/retention, soak and hardware capacity reports remain unfinished. Primary references and limits Design references: Stream Load, Unique Key concurrency, JSON precision, tablet identity/privileges, official fixture image. Product documentation is not project acceptance; see validation. Complete clusters/compute-storage separation, combined FE/BE faults, TLS, all JDKs, huge catalogs/transactions, adoption/repair/migration and capacity matrices remain pending. SQL modes and text validation Catalog, receipt and row-verification values use binary server-prepared MySQL parameters. The adapter forces useServerPrepStmts=true and emulateUnsupportedPstmts=false ; an unsupported protocol fails instead of silently reverting to literal interpolation. DDL comments contain safe internal identifiers only. Actual Doris4.1.3/Java8 EMPTY and NO BACKSLASH ESCAPES profiles passed quoted/backslash names, Unicode/emoji text, snapshot, CDC and session reconstruction. Malformed UTF-16 fails deterministically with DORIS TEXT ENCODING INVALID , rather than retrying invalid text indefinitely; see additional evidence. Sources: Doris prepared statements, string literals. After the binding change, current release9a087 also passed an actual MySQL8.4.13→PostgreSQL17.12+Doris4.1.3 pipeline with outage catch-up, worker kill, SQL repair/retry and missing-view isolation. The native mode/old-backup case used11667063; all14Doris adapter classes match9a byte-for-byte. See additional evidence for artifact and scope distinctions.

title: Controller and Agent lifecycle
text: Separate management entries and execution Agents 中文 · Global control · SDD contract The protocol4 separated profile passes348app/actual-JAR tests,76DOM and5x152controls,PG/MySQL stores,actual multi-database/two-target CDC,all-controller loss,store outage,pending accepting-entry recovery,nonroot processes and SQL role races.Automatic Agent takeover and complete journal/adapter/JDK matrices remain open. Evidence. Configuration role Registry role Responsibility --- --- --- COMBINED CONTROLLER WORKER Compatible management/local execution in one process CONTROLLER CONTROLLER UI/API,shared login,configuration and durable admission;execution capacity0 AGENT AGENT Fixed-owner execution,Worker supervision,observations and typed reads;HTTP probes only Activation Every member sets cluster.sharedAccess=true,sharedTasks=true,separateExecution=true and an explicit role. Control database,cluster.id,namespace and Base64 task key match; node IDs and private directories/volumes are independent. separateExecution=false keeps protocol3 combined behavior; defaults do not silently become separated deployments. Separation uses protocol4. Stop all old members normally and confirm STOPPED before upgrade; expiry/unreachability is insufficient. Preserve tasks,journals,reports,keys and directory UUIDs. Old programs refuse the new protocol; direct database downgrade is unsupported. An existing combined owner with tasks retains its original nodeId/directory when reopening as AGENT. A controller refuses an execution directory with tasks,including shared ownership hidden behind an empty replacement directory. Legacy local-to-global import remains a separate migration. Controllers cannot receive execution tasks. Create requests specify an Agent; the UI filters controllers and pages to find Agents. Committing transactions recheck role/ownership instead of trusting an earlier directory/role read. Linux The controller example uses8080;the Agent example uses8081. Adjust control connections and supply token,control credentials and task key environment values,then run independently: Use separate configuration copies/directories and distinct ports on one host. Supervise with separate systemd services; management service dependencies must not stop the Agent. Agent termination stops its own supervised Workers. Docker Build the current image first. Supply RIVOMESH TOKEN,RIVOMESH TASK KEY,RIVOMESH CONTROL URL,RIVOMESH CONTROL USERNAME,RIVOMESH CONTROL PASSWORD. The example assumes PostgreSQL control storage: It creates controller-a,controller-b,agent-a with three private volumes. Management ports bind loopback8080/8082;Agent probes bind8081. Browser access still needs HTTPS/proxy configuration for production cookies. Stopping management must not delete/stop Agent state. The file does not create the external control database. Helm and native Kubernetes Use the shared Secrets documented under global control,then install independent releases: Without Helm,adapt/apply native manifests A,B,Agent. Each release has one replica/private PVC. Add Agents with distinct releases/node IDs/volumes. Static rendering/invalid-setting checks exist;live Kubernetes/CSI/node-fault acceptance is separate. Recovery FAQ What if every management entry stops? The Agent independently reads the shared queue. The tested LOCAL/H2 profile continues CDC;management rejoin reads the same owner and authority. This does not relocate execution to another Agent. Does CDC survive control-store failure? In the tested LOCAL/H2 profile,the same Worker continues source capture and independent business writes. Management APIs/registration readiness refuse control without local-account fallback. Recovered storage permits renewed registration and observations. External-journal shared failures,other adapters and production topologies require their own profiles. Why does the Agent have no login page? Its HTTP endpoint serves GET /healthz and /readyz only;administration paths return404 AGENT PROBE ONLY. Use management entries;typed owner queries travel through shared storage. What if the Agent exits or is killed? Its Workers are affected;management shows pending/unknown. Restore original Agent directory,nodeId and keys;queued offline STOP is processed before restoring old RUNNING intent. Expiry does not prove process termination. Automatic takeover/stale-Worker fencing remain CP-04. Are Agent secrets least-privilege isolation? No. Agents remain in the trusted control domain;Workers filter controller environment variables. Roles do not establish tenant/OS isolation. Least-secret/external-identity work remains separately tracked. NODE ID IN USE after restart? SIGKILL leaves an old lease until expiry;never bypass the guard.Supervisors may retry normally;if another member keeps renewing,fix duplicate configuration. VALIDATION BARRIER MOVED immediately after configuration restart? Process liveness and already-equal rows do not establish a new journal claim.Check shared state and actual incremental catchup before retrying.The guard must not accept a moved cut;clearer startup readiness remains CP-06.

title: Failed transaction diagnostics
text: Failed-transaction diagnostics and manual recovery 中文 · SDD contract The UI supports destination phase summaries,original incremental retry,snapshot-part recovery and administrator transaction review. Bounded inspection/durable evidence now back explicit raw/normalized event pages. Manual skip and independent corrective entry remain unavailable. Common-cut report-driven repair is documented in managed repair;it is not failed-queue compensation. UI workflow 1. Open the paused destination in task details. Record destination ID,error generation,ACK,error code,phase and failed sequence when available. 2. For activation faults,check connectivity,credentials,permissions and metadata. For apply faults,check types,constraints and destination data. For projection faults,check mappings and historical schemas. For reconciliation faults,verify native receipts and journal ACKs before changing anything;do not manually advance positions. 3. Fix the cause and select “Resume this target.” The request binds its error generation,retrying the whole original incremental transaction or reconciling/resuming snapshot parts. Stale generations refuse. Pipeline resume and destination resume are distinct. 4. Check catch-up and run appropriate reconciliation. Accepted commands,live processes or matching ACKs alone do not prove business takeover readiness. Activation can fail before a transaction is identified,so no invented failed sequence is shown. Legacy pauses without trusted phase records remain Unknown. Corrupt diagnostics are visibly unavailable and raw inspection refuses. Equal SQLStates do not make activation and apply faults equivalent. Existing global task queries carry summaries through different management entries. Summaries contain only phase,sequence and failure epoch;no event IDs,row values,SQL or credentials. Existing task-view grants apply. Ordinary status does not gain raw-value access. Initial preparation/snapshot have dedicated diagnostics;legacy records may remain Unknown. Complete source connection/read/decode/DDL phases remain open. See native snapshot evidence. Accepted scope and evidence cover internal inspection,two-entry real SQL fault/restart and five-JRE foundation contracts;they do not accept the complete manual recovery workflow. Internal inspection limits Journal.inspectFailure(subscription, expectedErrorGeneration, maximumBytes) reads only a paused subscriber's next whole transaction. It binds stream generation,current epoch,configuration fingerprint,error generation and ACK and verifies raw/existing normalized hashes. It never connects to or activates business destinations,creates normalization,changes keyless identities or advances ACK. Missing complete boundaries refuse rather than being guessed. Raw and normalized payloads share a maximum4MiB budget;diagnostics have a separate16KiB limit. Stored-length checks and bounded character streaming enforce limits,with UTF-8 byte verification. Unconsumed normalization reservations may conservatively refuse a payload early. Oversize refuses the whole review rather than approving a truncated transaction. Streaming large-transaction review remains open. This low-level inspection is not an execution plan;managed access adds durable creation,authorization and audit. Its returned object alone is not durable evidence or approval. Paused ACKs pin history;resume can allow collection. UI review reads retained records. Manual native-checkpoint reconciliation,approval and gaps remain open. Preparation/snapshot faults explicitly refuse inspection as failed incremental transactions. FAQ Can I skip an error like a MySQL replica? Not yet. One source transaction can span tables/events. Future skip applies to a whole transaction for an explicit destination and requires native SKIP receipts,durable gaps and idempotent recovery. Editing ACKs/GTIDs or deleting logs breaks recovery guarantees. What if the destination committed but the response was lost? Automatic delivery verifies destination checkpoints,transaction IDs and projected-content hashes before repairing journal ACKs. Unknown outcomes stop/retry rather than authorizing skip. Manual compensation must reconcile first too. Can a source update fix an old transaction? It creates a new transaction;persisted old events remain unchanged. Fix the destination condition preventing old replay. Future compensation must use historical images and current destination state. Does restart clear an error? No. Pause,error generation and phase diagnostics persist. Explicit resume remains necessary. Healthy destinations may continue while the paused subscriber retains history and consumes quota. Can Unknown be treated as an apply error? No. Legacy records,corrupt diagnostics and capture/decode faults do not establish a known skippable transaction. Inspect source history,retention and historical configuration first. What if required binlogs were purged or cannot be decoded? Destination resume cannot recreate source history. Restore logs,use a qualified source retaining required history or prepare a new baseline/rebuild. Controlled gap recovery and all-affected-destination accounting remain open under RC-04/08. Can I patch destination rows directly? Synchronization assumes exclusive destination writes. Unplanned edits can affect constraints,keyless identities and replay. Typed UI corrective entry,drift checks and atomic compensation receipts belong to RC-06/07 and are not available yet.

title: Failed transaction evidence
text: Failed-transaction evidence storage 中文 · Contract · Recovery Storage/capture now backs managed review,including administrator/task authorization,audit and protocol5 gates. This page explains files/limits. Successful retention does not prove destination non-commit or authorize skip,compensation or takeover. Earlier internal acceptance is distinct from the current managed profile. Contents and identity Immutable evidence binds review/request IDs,actor/time,task,original execution node/directory,configuration revision,stream generation/epoch,error generation,ACK and whole-transaction hashes. It retains raw/existing normalized transactions and their referenced historical schemas. Missing normalization remains explicit;review does not normalize or change keyless identities. Schema lookup uses only referenced tableId/schemaVersion pairs,not the full catalog. Missing,corrupt or mismatched schemas refuse capture. Published evidence remains readable after journal collection. It records a historical observation;execution still requires fresh configuration,position,native receipt and drift checks. FailureEvidenceCapture.capture first checks an existing review ID against request,actor,revision,destination and error generation,returning the original result without requiring retained journal history. Changed content,identity or request parameters cannot overwrite the original. Private files and quotas - Defaults:256MiB directory budget,1000records,8MiB per record,configured through internal FailureEvidenceStore.Limits . Files,keys,authority and orphan temporaries count toward the budget;this is not total disk-block/database/backup capacity. - Directories use0700;created records,keys,authority and lock files use0600. Reject symlinks including parent paths. Preserve private permissions in installation and backups. - A random32-byte evidence.key authenticates records; authority.json binds original task/node/directory. Content hashes and strict JSON parsing refuse truncation,duplicate fields and trailing JSON. - Cross-process locking,private temporaries,file fsync,atomic publication and directory fsync protect publication/quotas. Busy locks refuse explicitly;callers retry the original request. - Full quotas refuse new evidence without deleting old records. Automatic expiry/GC/key rotation is not exposed. Orphan .pending files are not valid evidence,remain counted and are not silently deleted. Physical disk/power-loss acceptance remains open;unit tests do not establish it. Summaries and pages Summaries expose identity,phase,positions,hashes and event counts without row images or SQL. Raw/normalized events paginate separately,at most100events/256KiB per page. A single oversized event refuses rather than returning truncated images. Every page carries the immutable evidence hash and next index. Journal inspection still limits combined raw/normalized content to4MiB and historical schemas to2MiB. Streaming large-transaction review remains open. File/page limits do not bypass capture limits. FAQ Can a lost key be regenerated? No. Existing authority/evidence without the key refuses initialization;wrong keys fail signatures. Restore key,authority,evidence and original directory identity together,including private permissions. Can files be copied to another Agent for automatic takeover? No. Changed owner/directory identity refuses. Explicit migration,authorization and checkpoint handoff remain open. Does retention freeze destination commit status? No. Capture does not connect to or activate business destinations and never assumes non-commit. Manual native-checkpoint reconciliation remains RC-05. Is the file a skip plan? No. Native receipts,fresh state checks,approval,gaps and idempotent recovery are still required. Manual skip/independent corrective entry are not exposed.

title: Retain and review failure evidence
text: Managed transaction evidence review 中文 · Diagnostics · Files/quotas This workflow passes the documented bounded profile. Review only retains/reads historical evidence. It does not skip,compensate,change GTIDs or automatically resume. First deployment Configure all controllers and Agents using thefirst-release baselinebefore startup. Development-version in-place upgrades/automatic mode migration are unsupported. Linux,Docker,Helm and manual Kubernetes share identity/storage requirements. Metadata DDL requires appropriate privileges;restart recovery and missing-history refusal remain supported. Start from a paused destination 1. Sign in as ADMIN and check the paused destination's phase/error generation. Preparation/snapshot faults use their own recovery paths rather than failed incremental review. 2. Select “Retain transaction evidence.” The operation persists its review ID before capturing the whole head transaction/historical schemas.202means accepted only. After success,select “Review transaction evidence” in operation history. 3. Inspect original task revision,configuration fingerprint,owner/directory,source identity,GTID/log position,transaction/event range,historical tables,image availability and hashes. ACK/epoch are historical observations,not current destination commit proof. 4. Explicitly show raw or normalized events. Historical column names/types accompany before/after images. SQL NULL,JSON text null ,Not provided and Not applicable remain distinct. Expand raw details for internal row identities. 5. Page through complete events bound to the same evidence hash. Oversized events refuse rather than truncate. Missing retained normalization disables that view. OPERATOR/VIEWER cannot create/read evidence,including direct URLs. Raw values do not enter ordinary task status,operation results or audit bodies. Logout clears/closes review and stale responses cannot reopen old-session data. Both entries use the same durable command/original-owner query. Repeating the same request ID retains one review ID. Original-directory Agent recovery preserves evidence,including after journal GC. Unavailable original Agents/control stores refuse rather than returning invented local data. configurationRevision in the summary is the create action's original task revision. The configuration fingerprint is separate;this field is not a configuration-history restore reference. API mapping Create through the existing action route with X-Request-ID : Poll task operations for completion/ failureEvidenceId . Retry the original request parameters/ID. - GET /api/tasks/ task /failure-evidence/ id :administrator summary. - POST /api/tasks/ task /failure-evidence/ id /events :administrator pages with "view":"RAW","from":0,"limit":20 or NORMALIZED . - Cookie POSTs retain CSRF/Origin checks;Bearer APIs remain compatible. Stale generation/revision,authorization changes,corruption and limits refuse explicitly. Native checkpoint comparison and proven-commit confirmation New review operations attempt a read-only native checkpoint comparison for transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations. The operation retains the observation; the evidence dialog displays it: - Checkpoint not advanced : native progress equals journal ACK. This does not prove business data is absent. - Committed but unacknowledged : native progress is exactly ACK+1 and transaction ID/projected hash both match. Reconcile acknowledgment before any skip or compensation. - Unavailable/refused : display a safe problem code. Missing normalization, changed epoch/error generation, collected history, unavailable/unsupported destinations must not imply a commit verdict. Retained evidence remains readable. This is a historical observation made while retaining evidence. Opening old evidence does not query the destination; retain new evidence to compare again. Inspection neither activates targets nor advances ACK. A lagging target epoch is explicitly reported as requiring fencing before a later mutation. Older members returning no observation are shown as unavailable. Eligible administrators can use proven-commit confirmation;skip and compensation remain unimplemented. Follow RC-05 design. The bounded read-only profile passed. The managed confirmation bounded profile also passed;skip and compensation remain separate,and RC-02 historical scope is unchanged. FAQ and limits Does saving resume replication? No. Business data,ACK,GTID and pause intent remain unchanged. Fix the cause and explicitly resume separately. Can review edit or skip? No. Proven commits can be acknowledged through the separate confirmation workflow. Administrators can use separate reviewed operations for whole-transaction skip, compensation and target corrections. Why is creation unavailable to an administrator? Shared review may be disabled. Old profiles do not accept new commands;follow normal stop/upgrade steps for every member. Why no transaction or a changed generation? The target may have resumed,changed fault,lack a complete incremental head or lack historical schemas. Recheck state;do not advance positions manually. Why refuse a replaced directory/key? Evidence binds the original directory and HMAC key. Restore records,key,authority and directory identity together rather than substituting empty storage/new keys. Are files encrypted or automatically cleaned? Files use private permissions/HMAC integrity;business content is not encrypted by this store. Protect backups,volumes and accounts appropriately. Automatic cleanup,key rotation and an evidence directory management UI remain open;full quotas preserve old records and refuse additions.

title: First-release configuration
text: First-release configuration baseline No first release has been published. In-place upgrades between development candidates,old package aliases and automatic control-mode migration are unsupported. Internal format numbers are not released versions. Choose the control store,access mode,roles,keys and persistent directories before first deployment. Enable full managed recovery consistently across all members: Namespaces are created directly in the configured mode. Mismatches refuse immediately,even after every member stops. Existing development environments require a separately assessed new test baseline;deleting code history does not authorize clearing business data or moving only cursors. Linux/Docker use the same role configuration and independent persistent directories. Helm overlays controller/Agent values with values-recovery-skip.yaml ;manual Kubernetes can reference rivomesh-skip- .yaml . Examples do not establish liveK8s/CSI acceptance. Restart recovery,leases/epochs,authorization revocation and damaged/stale-backup refusal are current behavior rather than obsolete development compatibility. Replace superseded development implementations directly. Do not retain branches,configuration aliases or upgrade tests solely for old prerelease candidates. Documents describe current behavior;duplicate evidence/build snapshots converge on one verification baseline. Keep tests that validate current data correctness,recovery and security boundaries. Remove temporary containers,obsolete project images and intermediate builds once unused. V2/V3 execution consolidation is a separate pending batch. Seecurrent statusandSDD;cleanup does not close unrelated feature gaps.

title: Data-gap verification
text: Data-gap verification 中文 · Transaction skipping · First-release configuration Plans,approval,fresh scans and durable receipts are implemented for transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations. See SDD for acceptance progress. Verification neither repairs data nor reapplies skipped transactions,nor automatically resumes replication. Console workflow 1. Resolve differences and run a new complete common-cut comparison. Select a COMPLETE,MATCH report with sealed source data. An old report alone does not establish current target correctness. 2. Click “Select gaps and prepare verification” in the report. Choose a target and unverified gaps,enter a reason and maximum duration. A plan covers at most100 gaps/1000 affected tables;default300seconds,range1–86400seconds. 3. Open the prepared plan in “Transaction recovery and data gaps”. Review target,report,cut,table names,source counts,content roots,gap scope and duration. Tables are paged in groups of50. 4. Confirm scope and exclusive sync-service target writing,enter an approval reason,and choose “Approve scope and verify again”. ADMIN is required;202 only acknowledges command admission. 5. Inspect the resulting VERIFIED AT COMMON CUT receipt. It establishes reviewed table equality at that historical cut only. Original SKIP history remains and the task stays paused. Cutover requires separate checks. External application/administrator writes bypass this fence and invalidate its operating assumption. Planner and approver are separately recorded;different accounts are not mandatory. Management entries may differ;the original Agent uses its recoverable report directory. Moving only a cursor does not replace journals,reports or original records. API Require ADMIN,task/node grants and matching expectedRevision ;cookie sessions also require CSRF. Use a stable X-Request-ID . An unknown response is retried with the identical ID and original body,without changing reason/scope. Send POST /api/tasks/ task /actions : errorCount is task status error count ,the whole pipeline generation rather than a subscriber's error count. The command request ID becomes the plan ID. Read it through GET /api/tasks/ task /gap-verifications/ planId . After review,submit GAP VERIFY EXECUTE with the same target,current task revision and the plan's errorGeneration : Execution cannot select another report,gaps or duration. GAP VERIFY CANCEL carries no gap object. Inspect task operations and the original plan for final results. Responses exclude business row images. Gap sequence / next values are strings;never convert them to JavaScript floating-point numbers. Failure handling and FAQ Situation Handling --- --- GAP LIVE DATA DIFFERENCES Fresh scans still differ;no successful receipt is written. Resolve differences and obtain a valid report before review. Resume,moved cut/native checkpoint/schema Refuse;obtain a new comparison and plan rather than editing stored scope. GAP VERIFICATION PLAN CHANGED / GAP VERIFICATION RECORD CHANGED Restore consistent persistent state;missing history is never silently recreated. Agent/network interruption or unknown response Inspect the original receipt. Identical approval replay returns committed history without another scan/write;uncommitted source transactions roll back. Cancellation A request is not proof of rollback. GAP VERIFICATION CANCELLED CHECK RECEIPT requires reading the original receipt;commit may have completed. hasGaps=true , hasOpenGaps=false SKIP history exists with common-cut receipts;this is not live equality. gapCountLimited=true Counts are lower bounds from a bounded window. hasOpenGaps=null means unseen unresolved gaps are unknown;continue paging. Accepted loss Acceptance creates a gap,not equality. Fresh full affected-table comparison must pass before recording verification at a cut. Plans,original SKIP history and receipts remain in source-journal metadata. Native target receipts/business data are unchanged. Source transactions persist plans and atomically commit verification receipts with all selected gap links. First-release schemas are created directly without in-place prerelease-candidate migrations. Progress semantics Field Meaning --- --- captured sequence Captured incremental-log sequence as an exact decimal string covered sequence Minimum safe coverage across targets,including explicit skips subscriptions[].safeCoveredSequence Target acknowledgment coverage subscriptions[].contiguousDeliveredSequence Contiguous non-skipped prefix,stopping before the first historical SKIP subscriptions[].firstSkippedSequence First historical skip or null subscriptions[].progressSemantics SQL COMMITTED,BROKER ACCEPTED or MATERIALIZER ACKNOWLEDGED For SQL,the contiguous prefix represents ordered committed projections. Verification never changes SKIP into APPLIED. Broker receipt is not consumer completion;materializer acknowledgment is not visibility on every replica. New progress values are strings beyond JavaScript integer precision. Snapshot completion remains a separate state.

title: GaussDB index policy
text: Gauss index conversion, correctness, and application takeover Updated: 2026-11-14. 中文：Gauss 索引策略. See requirements and decisions for scope and open questions. Status: v3 implements ordinary secondary indexes and business UNIQUE downgrade; v2 still creates columns/PK only. IndexPolicy produces explicit actions and JdbcSink executes supported indexes on new tables. Expressions/prefixes/descending/special methods and existing UNIQUE/GSI require separate plans, never blind DROP. Business GSI model entries may become ordinary indexes; identity GSIs are not downgraded. Commercial distributed GaussDB still needs hardware acceptance. See the V3 manual. Accepted synchronization policy MySQL is authoritative. Only the synchronization service writes to targets during synchronization; applications may read them. Validate data and restore required constraints before application writes take over. For newly created Gauss business tables: Source object / target requirement Synchronization policy --- --- MySQL PRIMARY KEY Preserve stable row identity and uniqueness; never downgrade to an ordinary index Business secondary UNIQUE(email) or composite UNIQUE Create a nonunique ordinary index with corresponding columns/order; preserve compatible column definitions and NOT NULL Ordinary secondary index Create an ordinary index supported by the target GSI contemplated for secondary uniqueness or query acceleration Use an ordinary secondary index, without global routing/uniqueness guarantees Unique structure required for PK, row identity, or internal correctness Excluded from relaxation; choose compatible distribution/constraints or fail preflight Metadata transaction deduplication, owner/lease, and checkpoint uniqueness Preserve; business-index relaxation does not apply Existing target UNIQUE, GSI, FK dependencies, etc. Inspect dependencies and produce a difference/migration plan; do not automatically DROP or weaken An ordinary index cannot replace a PK. Replacing a global UNIQUE with UNIQUE(email, distribution key) is not equivalent: it allows duplicate email across distribution keys and still enforces a constraint that may be unnecessary during synchronization. This topic covers openGauss/distributed GaussDB. Other adapters may also relax incompatible business secondary UNIQUE constraints under declared policies. Preserve PK/candidate identity and internal correctness; analytical Unique Key/materialization identity is not an optional secondary constraint. See platform design. What UNIQUE(email) means Example source definition: Logical target example, not current generated output or a universal version-independent script: Omitting target UNIQUE does not itself create duplicates. Final correctness depends on complete replication. At the same fully applied source transaction boundary, each source PK should correspond to the same target row if: 1. Every source transaction is logged and captured completely, with FULL row images, correct ordering, and correct routing. 2. PK mapping is one-to-one; target PK comparisons do not merge distinct source keys. 3. Snapshot/CDC handoff has no gaps, and durable GTID/checkpoints plus idempotent application handle redelivery. 4. Business changes and apply checkpoints commit atomically; retries never skip failed transactions; stale owners are fenced. 5. No external writes, trigger side effects, lossy conversions, or accidental merging of source tables occur. Under these conditions, the source enforces email uniqueness and the target reproduces its rows. The target ordinary index no longer enforces email uniqueness. Retry idempotency relies on PKs and transaction checkpoints, not the email index. Removing UNIQUE is not a recovery mechanism. Preserve multiple NULLs allowed by the source; GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT( ) 1 alone is not a valid constraint check. Case, collation, trailing spaces, empty-string/NULL behavior, and type conversion can change equality semantics. Source uniqueness does not guarantee that a future target UNIQUE constraint will build successfully. Temporary duplicates during snapshot The current snapshot uses online chunks followed by log replay, not one database-wide point-in-time snapshot. For example, the scanner reads id=1,email=a ; a source transaction changes it to b and inserts id=2,email=a ; the scanner then reads id=2. Before catch-up, the target may contain two distinct PKs with email=a even though every committed source state was valid. Temporary secondary-key duplicates are not duplicate PK rows and must not cause data to be discarded. Complete ordered replay must restore the source state at the declared boundary. Snapshot/early catch-up output is not promised to be consistent; consumers requiring consistency wait for an agreed barrier and read protocol. Ordinary secondary indexes permit these intermediate states, which fits the current scan method. Preserving selected target UNIQUE constraints in a future design would require revisiting snapshot/replay semantics and constraint timing, not merely adding UNIQUE to generated DDL. Can GSI become an ordinary index? Yes, an ordinary index can be selected during new-table index planning to retain a basic access path on corresponding columns. This is a replacement with changed capabilities, not a lossless native conversion. MySQL has no Gauss GSI; keyword substitution in source DDL cannot implement it. Huawei documents GSI distribution independent of the base table. Its example contrasts an ordinary index visiting all DNs with GSI routing a qualifying lookup to one DN. This design therefore accepts possible extra cross-node query work and promises no equivalent performance. Verify exact version capabilities. CREATE GLOBAL INDEX, official query-plan example. Design consequences: - Ordinary indexes provide neither cross-DN global uniqueness nor GSI's separate distribution/covering design; changing an index does not redistribute its base table. - Retaining indexed columns does not preserve query plans, covering behavior, or JOIN performance. Validate representative queries with EXPLAIN . - A global structure required to enforce PK identity cannot be relaxed. Prefer distribution compatible with the PK; fail preflight when correctness cannot be preserved. - Existing GSI may support constraints or other dependencies. Migration must inspect ownership, dependencies, validity, and rollback paths before removal. Partition GLOBAL/LOCAL indexes describe partition coverage and must not be confused with distributed GSI. openGauss partition-index syntax is not evidence of GaussDB GSI capability. openGauss index documentation. Distributed business and metadata tables Relaxing business secondary constraints does not remove restrictions involving PKs, distribution/partition columns, or types. Distribution planning must be deterministic, explainable, and overridable, with an explicit write strategy for PK/distribution-key changes. Metadata requires its own design: deduplication keys, task IDs, stream ordering, and lease operations must satisfy distributed constraints, while business changes and local target checkpoints remain atomic. Do not delete UNIQUE(job id, transaction key) to avoid GSI, or infer source ordering from independent CN-generated IDs. The current metadata layout has not been validated on commercial distributed GaussDB and is not a deployment template for it. Planning and resumable execution Implementation requires these steps, not merely removing a UNIQUE keyword: 1. Discover source index metadata: PK/secondary classification, column order, prefix lengths, expressions, sort direction, visibility, and method. Persist a versioned conversion manifest. 2. Generate executable DDL and capability differences for the target product/version/mode, distribution/partitioning, and types. Deduplicate equivalent target indexes; use stable digests when shortening names. 3. Create columns and PKs before snapshot; persist definitions, policy, and fingerprints. Correct row identity comes first. 4. Prefer ordinary business secondary-index creation after initial catch-up, with bounded concurrency. CDC progress and index readiness are separate: streaming does not imply every index is READY. 5. Persist planned/started/succeeded/failed states and definition digests per target/table/index. After restart, inspect catalog definitions and validity before proceeding. Adapter-specific recovery must cover nontransactional DDL and invalid indexes left by online builds. 6. A matching name with a different definition is not success. Retain diagnostics and retry the object without resetting snapshot cursors or skipping business transactions. Pause a target if DDL failure compromises safe writes; a missing acceleration-only index may instead leave CDC running with a failed index phase. Report prefix, expression, FULLTEXT, SPATIAL, invisible, oversized, and unsupported-collation indexes individually. Initially automate only ordinary column-based B-tree-like indexes; explicitly list other objects as unsupported/manual work rather than claiming complete index synchronization. Do not silently expand a prefix index to the full column, which may exceed limits or change plans. Application takeover This is a planned operating procedure, not an existing automated command. Validate each target independently; simultaneous takeover of every target is unnecessary: 1. Freeze relevant source business writes and DDL; record a final source GTID barrier and eliminate dual-write entry points. 2. Wait for the target to apply through that barrier with no failed transactions, missing logs, or unfinished snapshot. Use proven target application progress, not shared capture GTID alone. 3. At the same frozen boundary, compare row counts, PK sets, chunk digests/required row values, and semantics for restored constraints. Retain original UNIQUE definitions in the conversion manifest. 4. Validate duplicates, NULLs, lengths, and dependencies using actual target equality rules; build required UNIQUE/FK constraints. If distributed constraints need GSI or redistribution, plan and validate that separately. Ordinary indexes during synchronization do not justify omitting constraints permanently after takeover. 5. Once all required constraints are valid and checks pass, stop or fence synchronization writes to that target, then permit application writes. Failure blocks takeover; repair and retry without deleting conflicting rows to force success. After application writes begin, the original one-way sync service cannot safely overwrite that target without coordination. Failback or bidirectional replication requires a separate design; GTID retention does not provide it. Other mirror targets may retain their own subscriptions, but after business moves to the new database the original MySQL source does not automatically receive those new writes. FAQ Will retries insert extra rows without UNIQUE? The keyed design uses PKs and transaction checkpoints; an ordinary email index does not deduplicate. No-PK support is now a first-release requirement but remains unimplemented. It needs candidate identity or consistent-baseline/multiset handling, not the keyed guarantee; see platform design. Are repeated email values always errors? No. Distinguish NULLs, comparison differences, and pre-catch-up mixed scan states. Judge against source definitions at a declared boundary; do not automatically delete rows. Are ordinary indexes always faster than GSI? No. They may reduce write maintenance but increase the DNs visited by queries. Measure actual workloads. Will existing target UNIQUE indexes change automatically? No. Current code does not do this; the design first produces an object/dependency migration plan. Constraint-owned indexes are not standalone objects to DROP blindly. Does an interrupted index build restart the snapshot? The design retains data checkpoints and resumes index work after catalog inspection. Implementation and fault validation remain pending. Is constraint restoration guaranteed to succeed? No. Actual validation and constraint creation gate takeover. Incompatible distribution/constraints or inconsistent data must block it. Acceptance checklist - Single/composite UNIQUE becomes nonunique with traceable ordering, nullability, and conversion manifests; PK/internal uniqueness remains intact. - Temporary email duplicates during online scans converge to the frozen source boundary; updates, deletes, PK changes, and transaction redelivery preserve rows. - Validate independently lagging targets; index failure on one target must not corrupt another target's state. - Test process death around index DDL, connection loss, uncertain responses, definition conflicts, invalid indexes, and stale owners. - Use real multi-CN/DN GaussDB to validate distribution compatibility, global row identity, transaction ordering, and ordinary-index plans; validate openGauss separately. - Before takeover, validate collations, empty strings/NULLs, target uniqueness, and the frozen barrier. Deliberate conflicts must block switching without discarding data. The current validation record excludes these new capabilities. It must not be used to claim index conversion or commercial distributed GaussDB acceptance. Doris business UNIQUE/GSI conversion uses nonunique inverted indexes; its internal UNIQUE KEY protects source row identity only. This is not GaussDB B-tree equivalence and does not preserve business uniqueness, collation or global routing. See the Doris handbook.

title: GBase 8c
text: GBase 8c destination GBASE 8C is an experimental adapter using the vendor's com.gbase8c.Driver and jdbc:gbase8c:// . 8a, 8c and 8s are separate product families ; PostgreSQL wire compatibility does not establish support for all three. 8a/8s remain separate planned adapters. The first profile targets V6 S1.3.0B19 ARM64, PG/UTF8; the first actual MySQL+PostgreSQL mixed snapshot/CDC/TIME/keyless/text-key/outage/catch-up/worker-kill/SQL-repair/missing-table acceptance passed. This applies to that profile and is not a full production matrix claim. See config/gbase8c-v3.yml. CLI and the Web v3 wizard share this adapter. Pre-create a PG-compatible UTF8 database and a synchronization account allowed to create schemas/tables/indexes and execute DML. The service does not change global compatibility settings or promote database nodes. Use a separate login. Native tests confirmed that initialization owner omm cannot connect remotely, and CREATEDB alone does not authorize schema creation inside postgres . An administrator can grant the required database scope: Existing schemas/tables need their own permissions or ownership. Synchronization does not require SYSADMIN. The fixture's CREATEDB attribute exists to create a negative compatibility-mode test database; pre-created production databases do not require copying that attribute. See the vendor permission guide. Session and data contract Every physical connection checks the metadata product and actual kernel version before vendor-specific SQL. It requires PG mode, UTF8, preserved empty strings and case/trailing-space-sensitive text comparisons. It sets session UTC, synchronous local commit and standard string escaping. Read-only endpoints raise a retryable connection error. Other compatibility modes require separate semantic and type plans. Quoted identifiers, row tables and primary keys are used. Keyless rows have internal occurrence IDs. JSON maps to JSONB; UINT64 to DECIMAL(20,0), wide decimals retain precision, binary maps to BYTEA, timestamps retain microseconds, and MySQL TIME becomes a signed INTERVAL. Generated values are taken from the source; complete target-side expression reconstruction is not promised. A native probe confirmed VARCHAR(100) holds 100 four-byte Unicode characters. Business changes and the target checkpoint share a local transaction and epoch fence. One unavailable target does not prevent independent targets acknowledging data. This does not imply cross-target distributed atomicity or protection against arbitrary physical backup rollback, split brain or external business writers. Index and distributed scope DOWNGRADE BUSINESS turns non-identity business UNIQUE into ordinary indexes. Simple business GSI conversion loses global uniqueness and routing. Primary, identity and internal uniqueness cannot be downgraded. Existing UNIQUE is not automatically dropped; expression/prefix/full-text/spatial indexes need a reviewed plan. Only the synchronization service may write destination business tables; validate and restore constraints before takeover. Distributed tables add distribution-key and unique-constraint restrictions: see the vendor SQL reference. A single-instance PG acceptance cannot establish CN/DN, DSS shared-storage, HA failover, cross-shard transaction or redistribution compatibility. Distribution-key changes, metadata/ownership placement, preserved UNIQUE and global indexes require independent planning and native verification. Recovery and FAQ - On downtime/network failure, retain journal/checkpoints and wait for the same writable destination. Size retained logs and source binlog retention for the outage. - SQL errors pause the affected subscription. Inspect/fix the cause and resume the original transaction. Manual skip/compensating data editing is not implemented. - Missing business tables isolate the affected target. Do not edit checkpoints; rebuilding or resnapshotting requires a separate plan. - Arbitrary nonempty adoption is rejected. Empty existing tables still need column/key/trigger/FK/index/ownership validation. - Unsupported live source DDL pauses safely; complete online schema evolution is pending. - The vendor filename is gbase8c-jdbc-3.0.0B02.jar , its embedded Maven version is 3.0.0 , and runtime DriverVersion contains an unresolved placeholder. Exact input identity uses fixed filenames and SHA-256, not that version string. Reproducible inputs Vendor downloads. Driver ZIP SHA-256: 3c2645993cd2e20a19941fc4d4bb5aba0f02ca378766543b6dd259a50c382721 ; JAR SHA-256: fe115f05124f6b9f37e49c829a0def28f7d09a6d871dd62a0c9f856b0aaa7e91 . The build verifies both, preserves vendor classes and a dedicated license resource, and checks Java 8-compatible bytecode. Native fixtures use separately obtained lawful vendor binaries. No database binaries/licenses are distributed in the repository. The local base image in tests/gbase8c/Dockerfile supplies Linux userland; the actual executable is verified vendor gbased , not openGauss pretending to be GBase. 中文 Native fixture reproduction / 原生夹具复现 Use Python 3.12+ and a lawful matching ARM64 vendor installer: Installer SHA-256: 6946abaa7666cbfadea3957682020262a102e52c6f7b4632d1f93fee9d3400b7 ; extracted B19 kernel SHA-256: 69663acfbb786c3f05cc434fb9f6d42806609b69c818c6e6ce0c4234748ad582 , matching its vendor checksum. The unified installer also contains a B10 kernel; this fixture explicitly selects B19.

title: Global task control
text: Global task control: activation, recovery and limits 中文 · SDD design 2026-11-17: an optional fixed-owner global profile now wires public HTTP, UI, shared configuration, durable commands and remote reads. Local control remains the default. CP-02/03 remain PARTIAL: legacy task import, complete business workflows, capacity and fault matrices are not fully accepted. Automatic owner relocation is separate. Activation Members share the control database, cluster.id, namespace, sharedAccess=true, sharedTasks=true and taskKey. Each has a distinct stable nodeId and private persistent task/data directories. taskKey is canonical Base64 text encoding 32 random bytes, supplied through protected environment configuration. Keep it out of task YAML. Never share controller.json. First activation requires empty task directories; existing registered tasks or YAML fail with GLOBAL TASK IMPORT REQUIRED. There is no automatic legacy import tool yet. Theplatform examplesupports Linux. Follow thefirst-release baseline;node modes,identities and keys must agree. Mode mismatches refuse without automatic migration or local fallback. Supply database credentials, token, key and node ID through the deployment environment. The example enables Secure cookies: expose HTTPS and configure the correct publicOrigin at the proxy. Helm and native Kubernetes The global Helm values reference existing Secrets: token in rivomesh-auth, and username/password/task-key in rivomesh-control-store. task-key contains the same Base64 key text on all members. Use separate releases, private PVCs and stable node IDs: Alternatively adapt and apply the native manifests A and B with kubectl apply -f. Independent controllers must not share a private directory. Static Helm/native parity and invalid-configuration checks exist; live Kubernetes/CSI, node-fault and rolling-upgrade acceptance remain open. Docker uses the same independent persistent-directory and key requirements. Acceptance fixtures leave no persistent preview. UI and configuration The session field taskControlScope=GLOBAL identifies this profile. Any entry lists authorized tasks with cursor pagination, owner/node state, global revision, Worker state, desired/active configuration and command results. Creation/import forms select the execution node; form import creates a new task and does not migrate old checkpoints. Unavailable owner execution is UNKNOWN, not stopped. Create/edit/restore/actions return 202 for durable admission only. Configuration history separates desired/active; the active pointer advances after successful owner application. Failed proposals preserve the old active configuration. Masked secret references work across entries. Connection previews, raw differences and repair-plan reads use expiring owner queries and cannot complete while the owner is offline. Complete filtering, log aggregation and real-browser visual/accessibility acceptance remain open. Global maximumTasks/maximumCommands differ from per-node maxTasks/maxRunningTasks. Defaults are 10000 global tasks and 1000 active commands; configuration ranges are resource guards, not hardware throughput promises. Queries are limited to 512KiB requests, 1MiB responses, 1–60 second lifetime, bounded readers and retained capacity. Admission and recovery PENDING is durable queueing. DISPATCHED saves the exact original local request/revision before invocation. ACCEPTED is local durable admission. SUCCEEDED/FAILED come from actual operation receipts. UNKNOWN requires reconciliation, not a success claim or reissue under a new revision. Startup restores receipt protection and validates local configuration against shared authority before scheduling. The latest startup fix scans all outstanding command pages, including undispatched STOP/PAUSE. Corresponding Workers cannot restore old RUNNING intent before local durable admission; older local operations may finish and stop commands receive priority retries. Rejection after authorization changes releases the block; uncertainty retains it. Focused tests and the application build pass; native business acceptance remains candidate-specific and does not retroactively change earlier evidence. TASK BUSY/OPERATION PENDING retain the original request. Outstanding receipts bypass ordinary 500-entry pruning. Cancellation has a parent and reserved capacity: cancel undispatched work atomically, reconcile uncertain delivery first, and perform actual cancellation after local admission. Success does not imply all targets rolled back. Offline STOP waits for the original owner. Restore its private directory/volume and keys; an empty directory cannot impersonate it. Default combined controllers stop their local Workers on exit. The explicit separated profile is covered by execution lifecycle; relocation, drain, scheduling and cross-Agent fencing remain separate work. Source MySQL primary promotion is a separate fault scenario from controller-owner takeover. Operations FAQ How do I distinguish accepted from executed? Inspect deliveryStatus, status, code and actual Worker/target checkpoints for the same request ID. HTTP 202 is not business commit evidence. Does refresh or another entry preserve login? Shared sessions restore identity subject to cookie domain, Secure, SameSite, expiry and revocation. Different domains require correct proxy/session configuration. Can A stop an offline owner? A durably queues STOP. It stays pending/unknown until the original owner supplies an actual receipt. Heartbeat expiry does not prove process termination. Can I edit owner fields, delete root tables or use an empty directory? No. Authenticated metadata, counts, private-directory identity, receipts and configuration projections reject missing/substituted authority. Does control-store failure fall back to local accounts? No. Management refuses control without shared authority. Existing data-process behavior follows its journal/lease/target protocol; management availability does not establish complete data-plane fencing. What belongs in backups? Coordinate the control database, every private directory, logs/reports/local journal, external journal if selected, and original keys. Restoring just a cursor or old control snapshot is insufficient; automated coordination and old-backup fault matrices remain open. What is already evidenced? Earlier candidates cover real PostgreSQL/MySQL control stores, two independent JVMs, HTTPS/shared login, A creating B-owned tasks and offline commands. Configuration fixtures also invoke real TaskService with fixture Workers. The startup fix and real cross-node business CDC are under additional acceptance. These do not establish all cluster, adapter or hardware profiles. Why is no persistent preview running? The user requested temporary fixtures only. They remove their own containers/volumes and leave unrelated resources untouched.

title: Apache Hive
text: Hive destination, recovery and FAQ 中文：Hive V3. Example: hive-v3.yml. Status The first independent native and actual mixed recovery profiles passed; the catalog retains an experimental label. CLI/Web V3 configuration, isolated JDBC, native HiveServer2 checks, ACID ORC history and latest-version views are implemented. Hive4.0.1/Java8 independent acceptance covered PK moves, keyless multiplicity, precision, lost-confirmation replay, case-folding, restart and older nonempty backup refusal. Actual MySQL8.4.13→PostgreSQL17.12+Hive passed snapshot/CDC, independent Hive outage and catch-up, worker SIGKILL resume, SQL constraint repair/retry, missing-view isolation and truthful pause fences. The final artifact/worktree-assets gate passed too; see evidence. This does not accept every Hive version, cluster or production capacity profile. The first fixture is official apache/hive:4.0.1 ARM64, one HiveServer2, persistent embedded Derby and local warehouse. It is not a production/HA deployment. HDFS/S3, external Metastore, Tez, Kerberos, TLS, clusters and other JDKs remain unverified. Layout and consistency Hive is a versioned analytical destination, not the transactional JDBC sink or a Journal. Each source table has a managed ACID ORC history table in metadataSchema . A view with the source table name in the mapped database selects the latest internal identity/version, filters tombstones and exposes source columns only. A primary-key move writes an old-identity tombstone plus a new row. Identical keyless rows retain separate normalized identities. Retries may leave duplicate physical versions; the business view should expose one current row per identity. History row count is not source row count. Only Rivomesh writes this layout; do not edit history, ownership properties or tombstones. One source transaction can span multiple Hive statements/tables: cross-table source transaction visibility is not atomic . JDBC commit is not an atomic business-data/checkpoint boundary here. An unfinished snapshot or backlog is not a cutover barrier, and this layout cannot directly take over OLTP writes. Types Normalized source type Hive storage --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 BOOLEAN / BIGINT UINT64 DECIMAL(20,0), bounded to unsigned 64-bit DECIMAL precision ≤38 DECIMAL(P,S), refusing overflow or rounding DECIMAL precision 38 STRING preserving digits and declared scale FLOAT32 / FLOAT64 FLOAT / DOUBLE; non-finite values refused STRING / JSON / DATE / TIME / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP STRING; not native JSON/temporal semantics BYTES / GEOMETRY base64 STRING preserving decoded bytes Generated columns retain evaluated values for expressions already supported by the source adapter; expressions are not recreated in Hive. Reassess comparison, ordering and query functions for the destination types, especially wide decimal strings. Full row images and explicit missing-vs-null checks remain required. First-profile names use ASCII letters/digits/underscore, cannot start with a digit, and are at most128 characters; mapped databases also follow common configuration length limits. Unsupported source names are not silently rewritten. rivomesh columns are reserved. UNIQUE, GSI and ordinary indexes Hive removed its old indexing feature from3.0; there is no equivalent ordinary B-tree conversion here. Official index documentation. Business secondary indexes are explicitly omitted. Review the differences and set acknowledgeIndexOmission: true ; initialization refuses secondary indexes without that acknowledgement. Source business UNIQUE is not enforced in Hive. GSI global routing, uniqueness, covering layout and performance are not retained. ACID/ORC/bucketing are not substitutes. Internal identity/version correctness is preserved. Convergence assumes an authoritative source, exclusive destination writes, complete catch-up and identity-preserving conversions; see index policy. Connection and deployment Require hive.txn.manager=org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.lockmgr.DbTxnManager , hive.support.concurrency=true , hive.query.results.cache.enabled=false , and managed full-ACID ORC tables/views. Operate Metastore, warehouse, transaction cleanup and compaction; session flags alone are insufficient. Hive transactions. Only direct binary jdbc:hive2://host:port/database is accepted, with optional auth=noSasl none and ssl=true false . Discovery, HTTP, Kerberos, URL credentials, initialization scripts and arbitrary session options are refused. Credentials use separate fields/environment references. noSasl is a matching-server option, not the production security default. TLS is configurable but not accepted by native testing yet. queryTimeoutSeconds is1–1800 (default300). Binary socket timeout is bounded to5–120 seconds and internal connect retries are0. A timeout does not prove the statement was absent. Default SQL/response limits are4MiB/16MiB, at most10,000 returned rows; overflow fails rather than confirming truncated results. Events also obey maxMessageBytes . Use a dedicated writer with private metadata-table DDL/read/write and property/description/definition access, plus mapped view DDL/read. Minimum grants depend on the authorization plugin and remain to be verified. Readers should access business views only. check is read-only and cannot prove write permissions. Its hiveIndexPlans entries expose per-table index actions, required acknowledgement and columnStorage types; omission is never reported as an ordinary-index conversion. A pinned standalone Hive SDK runs in a private classloader without replacing core logging/Jackson/Guava. First use extracts and verifies about42MiB under a private java.io.tmpdir cache. Read-only Docker/K8s filesystems need a restricted writable temporary volume; do not share an untrusted cache. Confirmation and recovery Implementation writes versions, reads back actual identity/version/tombstone/values, writes and reads a target receipt, saves Journal transport progress, then advances the destination transaction checkpoint. Physical row count alone cannot confirm an uncertain write. Reconnect checks ownership, layout, view definition, resource properties and the latest receipt. Established missing objects are not recreated at old progress. Resource UUID is a Rivomesh Metastore property, not independently authenticated storage identity. Coordinate Metastore, warehouse and Journal backups. Arbitrary partial-table/file rollback, forged metadata or partial history loss are not claimed to be fully detected. The first independent native case passed server restart and refusal of an older nonempty Metastore+warehouse backup while Journal retains newer progress; see the exact release and scope in evidence. Connection failures retry by classification; deterministic structure/permission/data errors pause this destination. Resume retries original data, without changing GTIDs or silently skipping. Pause cannot establish that every in-flight Hive request has been cancelled. Journal ACK-based reclamation does not reclaim Hive history. Monitor history, tombstones, receipts and ACID delta files separately. Receipt compression, safe history GC, compaction soak and hardware sizing remain unfinished. FAQ Why append versions instead of ordinary UPDATE/DELETE? History, versions and tombstones support snapshot replay, uncertain requests, PK moves and keyless identity under one layout. Read the view rather than the physical table. Can Hive take over the application? This analytical layout has neither source cross-table atomicity nor enforced business UNIQUE. Takeover needs a separately designed data model, reconciliation, barrier and constraints. Does Hive block other destinations? Delivery threads are independent; other destinations can progress while Hive is unavailable. Unconfirmed data retains shared Journal space and eventually causes capture backpressure at quota. The first mixed profile passed; Journal exhaustion and the wider fault matrix remain unverified. Can an existing nonempty table be adopted? Arbitrary adoption/overwrite is not implemented. Ownership or shape mismatch is refused. Live DDL, nonempty adoption and repair require later workflows. How is the native case reproduced? After building, run bash tests/hive-materializer-run.sh . It operates only its own named volumes and stops the server before coordinated Metastore/warehouse backup/restore. Failed raw logs stay in target/ ; inspect actual scenario coverage rather than relying on a marker alone. The fixture uses HIVESERVER2 PID DIR on a dedicated ephemeral runtime mount to avoid a stale PID matching a new process after container restart. Metastore and warehouse remain persistent volumes. This fixture correction is not a production Hive HA implementation. Query cache and consistent reads The mixed fixture returned three detail rows but a cached COUNT0. A fresh session with only query-results cache disabled returned COUNT3 while stats optimization remained enabled. This observation does not establish the same problem for every Hive release/deployment. The first supported profile requires the server default and all reader sessions to use hive.query.results.cache.enabled=false ; the writer session must also disable it. Read-only preflight and write-time checks refuse enabled cache with HIVE QUERY CACHE DISABLED REQUIRED , without silently changing global settings. Disabling cache only on the writer cannot protect other readers. Do not re-enable it in application connections or manually add rows based on stale cached counts. Correct server/reader settings before check/resume; this does not require resetting data, task identity or checkpoints. The original cache-enabled mixed run was explicitly aborted and is not accepted complete recovery. The cache-disabled profile passed independent materialization/restart/older-backup refusal; the frozen-release complete mixed run passed too; see evidence.

title: Implementation status
text: Current implementation status The first release is not published. Java/Maven namespace: io.github.rivomesh . SDD · Tasks · 中文. 48 requirements: 13 DONE,30 PARTIAL,5 NEW;35 open . Each accepted item is limited to its declared profile rather than every product/version/deployment combination. Accepted Scope Result --- --- CP-01 Unified registry,roles,versions,heartbeat and ownership SE-01–05 Reload persistence,expiry/revocation,secure cookies/CSRF,cross-entry sessions and API identity rules CP-07 Separated control/execution;bounded original-Worker continuity during management outages RC-02 Durable transaction evidence,authorized pagination,historical schemas and images RC-05 Native commit verification and acknowledgment recovery without reapplying rows RC-03 Complete cross-database skip,native commit/source ACK failure,original-Agent SIGKILL/reopen and cross-entry recovery;pauses/gaps retained RC-08 Durable gaps,reviewed verification,cross-entry approval/cancellation and honest incremental progress;bounded SQL profile RC-06 Before-image compensation with cross-entry approval and explicit resume. Bounded SQL profile RC-07 Typed entry, JSON import, before/after preview and cross-entry approval. Bounded SQL profile The single verification baseline retains scoped provenance rather than repeated development snapshots. Cleanup validation is distinguished from earlier acceptance. Existing capabilities and limits Capability Current boundary --- --- Replication MySQL multi-database mappings/fan-out,table creation,chunked snapshot-to-stream,durable progress,keyless/JSON/supported generated columns Management Bilingual wizard,configuration revisions,isolated Workers,durable cross-entry commands,accounts/grants/audit Compare/repair Common-cut row comparison and reviewed repair plans;bounded MySQL/PostgreSQL profiles Gap verification Reviewed plans,administrator confirmation,fresh scans,atomic receipts and cross-entry cancellation;bounded PG/MySQL,see guide for acceptance Transaction compensation Administrator review and approval for PostgreSQL and MySQL with atomic target receipts and original transaction replay. See the operator guide Relational targets Actual MySQL/PostgreSQL/openGauss profiles;experimental DM/Kingbase/GBase8c profiles;OceanBase full recovery and distributed GaussDB remain open Analytical targets Initial ClickHouse/Doris/Hive materialization/recovery;production clustering,security/performance remain open Messaging Kafka/Pulsar/RabbitMQ/RocketMQ/Classic/Artemis/Redis Streams/NATS JetStream have bounded confirmation/recovery profiles;complete cluster/TLS matrices remain open Deployment Linux,Docker,Helm,native Kubernetes YAML;liveK8s/CSI/node-fault acceptance remains open Java Java8 build baseline;partial five-JRE profiles,not the full source/target/driver/TLS/recovery matrix See design,console operations and product guides for constraints. Protocol/data-format numbers identify internal modes,not compatibility promises for unreleased builds. Cleanup Historical-binary probes,automatic control-mode migration and duplicate development snapshots are removed. Namespaces are created in the configured mode and refuse mismatches without silent migration/fallback.73 affected contracts pass. SDKs are installed in the Maven cache,so application-only iterations avoid rebuilding them. The V2/V3 execution branches,wizard and configuration fixtures still share dependencies;their consolidation is a separate pending batch. Business data and current state-integrity checks were not removed. Next work 1. Distributed recovery jobs and recovery protocols for other destinations. 2. Automatic Agent relocation,draining,global diagnostics and storage reachability. 3. PostgreSQL/Oracle sources,MySQL8.2 and complete5.7/8.0/8.4 profiles. 4. Distributed GaussDB and complete vendor/messaging/analytical production matrices. 5. Large transactions/catalogs,hardware benchmarks,liveK8s,complete JDK matrix and bilingual docs.

title: 金仓 Kingbase
text: Kingbase destination and FAQ 中文：金仓 V3. Example: kingbase-v3.yml. Scope and connection V3 configuration, CLI, explicit mappings, independent fan-out workers and the bilingual wizard accept product: KINGBASE . The first profile targets PG compatibility mode and remains EXPERIMENTAL . The first Java8/Kingbase V009R001C001B0025 PG/UTF8 native transaction and MySQL8.4.13+PostgreSQL17.12 mixed recovery profile passed; see evidence. Existing PostgreSQL results do not prove Kingbase compatibility. Other modes, RAC/distributed products, all versions and capacity remain pending. The pinned Java8 driver is cn.com.kingbase:kingbase8:9.0.1 , with com.kingbase8.Driver and jdbc:kingbase8:// , normally port54321. The vendor namespace coexists with PostgreSQL. Maven Central's vendor POM declares Apache-2.0; a complete distribution license/NOTICE review is still required. Every physical sink connection checks the actual product, version() , SHOW database mode , UTF8 encoding, empty-string preservation, case/trailing-space comparisons and writability before metadata access. It sets UTC, standard strings and synchronous commit=on . Only pg passes. The service never changes compatibility mode, global settings or database roles. Local synchronous commit still requires reliable server storage and suitable replication configuration; it does not prove multi-node failover durability. Have the DBA provision a UTF8 database, account and writable endpoint first. Each MySQL database explicitly maps to a schema within that Kingbase database. Rivomesh may create mapped schemas/tables/indexes and its metadata, but does not install the database or provision accounts. Provide metadata access and relevant schema/table/index creation plus business/checkpoint read/write privileges. A connection check does not prove all DDL/DML privileges. Use MYSQL PASSWORD / KINGBASE PASSWORD environment references or protected configuration. In the UI choose V3 and KingbaseES(PG), then explicit mappings. V2 does not enable this adapter. Linux, Docker, Helm and native Kubernetes use the same task document; deployment manifests do not deploy Kingbase. Data, indexes and recovery Business changes and the destination checkpoint commit in one local transaction, with metadata row locks and epoch fencing. An uncertain commit is resolved by rereading the destination checkpoint. Other targets acknowledge independently; this is not a distributed atomic commit. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery; cross-host worker takeover requires an already-supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journal. An unverified Kingbase journal backend is explicitly rejected. Keyless tables gain rivomesh row id to retain duplicate multiplicity. Supported generated expressions follow source-adapter support and their values become ordinary destination columns. UINT64 uses DECIMAL(20,0), decimals retain declared precision, JSON uses JSONB, binary uses BYTEA, microsecond times use TIMESTAMP(6), and signed/over24hour MySQL durations use INTERVAL. Procedures, triggers, foreign keys, partition layouts and arbitrary generated expressions are not automatically reproduced. DOWNGRADE BUSINESS turns business UNIQUE into ordinary indexes; primary/actual identity keys remain unique. Plain BTREE/simple business GSI can use the ordinary-index plan, losing global routing/global uniqueness. Expression, prefix, descending, fulltext and spatial methods require a separate plan. Downgrading assumes valid source constraints, complete ordered replication and exclusive synchronization writes. Reconcile and rebuild required constraints before takeover. Existing UNIQUE constraints are never silently dropped. Nonempty/incompatible targets require an adoption plan; the complete automated takeover workflow remains pending. Transient connection failures back off and reconnect; other sinks continue until journal backpressure applies. Deterministic SQL failures pause only that subscription. Repair the cause, then resume in the UI or with resume config/kingbase-v3.yml kingbase-business errorGeneration using the current status value and the same java -jar ... prefix. This retries the original transaction. Restart does not skip a pause. Missing tables/ownership/checkpoints refuse reuse of old progress; normal resume cannot repair lost data. TIME and native acceptance scope MySQL TIME is a signed duration, not a java.sql.Time/LocalTime wall clock. V3 snapshots and binlog events normalize it as [-]HH:MM:SS.ffffff . The pinned0.30.3 SDK uses duration overrides for ordinary/extended INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE row events; other fields retain its existing codecs. Native tests cover TIME2 precision0..6, negative fractions, over24hours and keyless identity. V2's accepted type range is unchanged. The real pipeline compares integer microseconds for positive/negative25hours, every fractional precision and negative1microsecond. Boundaries/malformed binary have unit coverage. Source reference SQL uses TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND,...,ADDTIME(...)) ; this environment's integer TIME TO SEC result and default four-place SQL division are unsuitable microsecond oracles. This Kingbase version returns float8 from EXTRACT(EPOCH), so readback first casts to NUMERIC(20,6), then compares integer microseconds. A generic duration-text mapping does not imply native TIME acceptance for every other adapter. The same actual release also passed cross-schema business/checkpoint rollback, replay, alias ownership, old-epoch refusal, writable checks, PostgreSQL masquerade refusal, snapshot/CDC, target outage while PostgreSQL continues and subsequent catchup, worker SIGKILL preserving generation/snapshot, separate SQL constraint repair/retry on both targets, persistent SQL pause through restart, missing-table isolation and final transactional fences. Other versions/modes, primary/replica clusters/routing, TLS, other JDKs, old nonempty physical backup restore, power loss, soak and hardware capacity remain pending. Existing custom column collations and application takeover require separate assessment. FAQ - Other compatibility modes? They need separate semantics, catalog/type adaptation and native acceptance. Changing an existing instance's mode is not an automatic compatibility fix. - Product/mode mismatch? Check the actual endpoint and SHOW database mode . Do not disguise it as a PostgreSQL target to bypass validation. - SQL ASCII or other encoding? Older vendor images may initialize SQL ASCII. Have the DBA provision a UTF8 database or migrate encoding, then recheck; Rivomesh does not rewrite database encoding in place. - Read-only endpoint? A retryable connection error waits for a writable primary. Database operations perform promotion and endpoint routing; do not reset checkpoints. - String comparison rejected? Check case/trailing-space settings. This profile requires distinct comparisons and never changes global comparison rules. - Existing rows/constraints? Use an explicit adoption plan. Do not clear metadata or drop constraints to continue an old task. - Concurrent business writes? The downgrade profile requires exclusive synchronization writes. Bidirectional conflict handling and the takeover workbench remain pending. - Database installation/license? Supply a properly licensed vendor build for the architecture. Rivomesh does not distribute database binaries/licenses or bypass authorization. Test containers do not require privileged mode. Reproducible native fixture and references With a lawful compatible image available, run bash tests/kingbase-pipeline-run.sh ; override RIVOMESH KINGBASE IMAGE for the same-layout build.
