The test uses actual release-JAR workers with isolated MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17/Kingbase services and removes only its own project/volumes. Initialization explicitly selects PG/UTF8 without case-insensitive initialization, running the native server as the image's kingbase user, without sudo/systemd/privileged. Different image layouts require fixture changes; replacing a version tag alone is not acceptance. - Official JDBC guide - Official Docker guide - Official parameter guide - Pinned JDBC POM

title: Managed repair
text: Managed data repair The first managed workflow passed real HTTP/Worker/database acceptance across LOCAL/H2 and external MySQL/PostgreSQL/openGauss journals,with MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 business destinations. Evidence. Full vendor,cluster,capacity and security acceptance remains incomplete. Workflow 1. Complete V3 row validation, keep the task paused and open its differing report. 2. Explicitly select differing destination/table pairs and create a plan. Initial profiles are MySQL/PostgreSQL,with a200table selection ceiling. Nothing is selected by default. 3. Open Review repair plan. Check destinations,tables,missing/extra/changed counts,creator and budgets. Explicitly check confirmation and execute. The browser sends the exact server-read plan hash rather than constructing business changes. 4. Inspect job results/target commit receipts. After failure/cancellation,review and retry the same plan;committed tables resolve from receipts without repeating DML. 5. Explicitly resume only after review and obtain a fresh validation when appropriate. Repair does not resume replication,change historical differences to MATCH or authorize cutover. Only authenticated ADMIN may create,review,execute or cancel. The server derives actor identity from authentication. Task/config revisions,request identity,plan hash,report seal and physical checkpoints constrain execution. Durable work and cancellation Admission persists the explicit scope,report and predetermined plan UUID before queuing. Restart reuses that identity. A saved plan with an unfinished controller operation is loaded and checked against its original creator,time and scope. A bounded maintenance queue is separate from normal controls;each task has at most one pending operation. Cancellation persists first,then interrupts the worker. Checkpoint/dependency waits and target scans/DML observe interruption. The current uncommitted table rolls back;previous commits remain. A cancellation can race a successful commit,so a cancelled result does not prove that nothing changed. Review/retry the same plan to resolve native receipts. Completion records per-table counts,original checkpoints and whether a prior attempt committed. Controller audit links authenticated actor,request and plan hashes. Raw business values never enter operations/audit. CLI actor assertions retain their separate host-trust model. The controller data directory contains operations,plans and sealed row reports;an external journal does not replace it. Persist/back up this directory for Linux,Docker and K8s. Local disk loss,multiple controllers on a shared PVC and live K8s node faults require separate acceptance. Never bypass identity/hash checks while restoring older files or metadata. Dependency refusal Plan creation and each table mutation check dependencies. Initial execution rejects incoming/outgoing foreign keys and triggers. PostgreSQL also rejects row security,partitions/inheritance and extra rewrite rules,and takes a table lock during these checks. Nothing is automatically disabled or dropped. MySQL trigger metadata requires TRIGGER privilege;an empty result with insufficient privilege cannot establish absence. See the official MySQL8.4 documentation. Initial visibility checks conservatively require direct global SELECT and TRIGGER grants and reject observed partial revokes. Role-only/schema/table-level combinations are not resolved yet and may return REPAIR METADATA VISIBILITY REQUIRED. Use an organization-reviewed migration account/profile rather than bypassing inspection. The synchronizer must remain the exclusive business writer. Arbitrary concurrent DDL/external writes are outside this contract. Changed roots produce REPAIR TARGET DRIFTED and require a new validation/plan. These checks do not establish arbitrary vendor/procedure/dependency coverage. API Use existing authentication,X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision with POST /api/tasks/TASK ID/actions: The202response already persists operations[].repair.planId. Wait for REPAIR PLAN READY,then GET /api/tasks/TASK ID/validations/REPORT UUID/repairs/PLAN UUID. This review projection contains counts/budgets,no raw rows or guarantee of current eligibility. Execution requires controller desired PAUSED. Cancel with REPAIR CANCEL and no repair payload. Idempotent replay uses the original request ID,body,revision and identity. A new request with a stale revision is rejected before creating another job. FAQ and boundaries A reviewed plan can become ineligible:execution rechecks current data,schema,configuration and pause cut. Wrong hashes are refused by the executor;stale revisions are refused at admission. Retry the same plan to resolve commits after cancellation. A complete real-time progress catalog,independent receipt browsing,report/scratch retention and cleanup remain pending. This mode requires a common cut. For a failed transaction, see compensation or reviewed skip. Nonempty adoption, constraint restoration and cutover remain open. Plans display default CLI repair budgets;UI budget editing is not implemented. Full vendor/version/cluster/capacity/security/controller-HA matrices remain incomplete. COMMON CUT foundations · Managed validation Development note:the existing general shape guard initially rejected triggers before the repair-specific check,producing a generic console failure. The guard remains intact;repair dependency checks now run first to return the explicit refusal. The corrected specified profiles pass;the failure and correction remain in the evidence.

title: Managed validation
text: Managed data validation The first management workflow supports SQL destination selection, time/staging budgets, durable background jobs, cancellation, sealed-source target retries and per-table summaries. Validation does not change business rows; see managed repair for the subsequent reviewed workflow. Constraint rebuilding and business cutover remain open. Consult transaction skipping for its separate SQL recovery profile. Managed HTTP/database acceptance is separate; earlier CLI/barrier acceptance cannot establish it. Use the console 1. Complete V3 snapshots, run the local Worker and verify shared RUNNING state. Selected destinations must be able to reach the common cut; unselected destinations can be paused/offline. 2. As ADMIN, select transactional SQL destinations under Data validation. Messaging/analytical destinations are excluded. First native row profiles cover MySQL/PostgreSQL; other SQL product versions/modes require separate acceptance. 3. Set source-gate, source-read and per-target-table deadlines plus logical/per-row budgets. Gate maximum is120seconds, reads24hours, rows32MiB. Total logical budget must be at least four times the row budget and includes source, destination and keyless identity records. Physical storage is additional. 4. Start comparison. After checking the current configuration revision, scope, report ID and budgets are persisted before execution in a separate background queue. Establishing the cut briefly blocks MySQL instance writes; business writes can continue after gate release while replication retains its durable pause. 5. Follow operation history, then open the report. Results show source/target counts and missing/extra/changed rows per table,50table results per page. A historical result does not establish current equality. 6. Inspect results/shared state and explicitly resume using the current error version. Validation never clears/repairs business tables, rebuilds UNIQUE or transfers write ownership. Cancel and recover Cancel is a durable request, not resume. Owned read connections/locks are aborted and complete sealed source data is retained. The response does not guarantee release at an exact millisecond:driver/connect/network timeouts also matter. Observe task state and database sessions. Cancellation before establishing a barrier can leave shared RUNNING state; the controller stops its local Worker and displays actual shared state. Once a barrier is established, cancellation never bypasses PAUSED. A sealed source allows Retry target comparison after loading the report. Original configuration/positions/epoch/physical target checkpoints and source integrity are checked; partial destination scans are discarded and reread, even with the source offline. The report's staging budget is retained; retries default to ten minutes per target table. Existing-report quota expansion and richer retry planning remain pending. An incomplete source MVCC view cannot survive process loss. Keep the failed report, inspect/explicitly resume as appropriate, and establish a new cut. Never mix source views or rewrite report hashes/GTIDs. Controller restart can reuse a report ID when complete source data survived but the operation completion did not; without a complete source view/local Worker, it fails explicitly rather than resuming the shared pipeline. One validation runs at a time; ordinary controls use a separate pool. Access, audit and storage ADMIN starts/cancels/retries; OPERATOR/VIEWER read summaries only for granted tasks. Cross-task access is hidden. Mutations require current revision and request ID; replay does not create another job. Previously accepted asynchronous work can continue after authorization changes; subsequent requests use current grants. Audit records actor, task, report ID, request hash and acceptance/completion/cancellation/read events. Corresponding audit writes are required before the HTTP response. Raw business values are excluded from summaries/history. Reports live under platform.dataDirectory/validations/ taskId / reportId . Private plaintext H2 files need protected persistent disk/PVC and coordinated backup; no encryption/external immutable anchor is provided. The console retains approximately40recent operations per task. Older files remain and known report IDs are readable through the API; full report catalogs/retention, large-directory pagination and controller HA remain pending. Local file locking is not cluster HA. API POST /api/tasks/ taskId /actions with X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision : Retry uses VALIDATE RETRY and validation: "reportId":" UUID ","targetMillis":600000 . Cancel uses VALIDATE CANCEL without validation input. GET /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId reads a summary. VALIDATION REPORT NOT CREATED means inspect the operation failure; VALIDATION REPORT BUSY means retry after the active scan. Core contract and FAQ / 中文 Job recovery paths First native managed acceptance passed LOCAL/H2 and external PostgreSQL/MySQL/openGauss journals with MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 destinations, including cancellation during an actual relation-lock wait, sealed-source retry and report/audit persistence across controller restart. See evidence and failure corrections. Administrator difference details For a completed report, ADMIN can open differences per target/table, page by identity hash, then explicitly reveal raw values. Stored source column names/types accompany expected/actual cells. An absent row is distinct from a present SQL NULL cell. Keyless source/target occurrence IDs are displayed without generating replacements. POST /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /differences with "target":"postgres","tableId":" table ID ","after":"","limit":25 returns items/next; maximum limit is100. POST .../values with the target/table and identityHash returns columns and expected/actual cells. Null for an entire side means absent row; cell value:null means SQL NULL. OPERATOR/VIEWER remain limited to summaries. Before releasing values, the server checks difference hashes, raw-row checksums and row identity and requires report/scope-linked audit. Business values never enter audit/controller operations. The API checks total UTF-8 raw JSON lengths before fetching CLOBs and refuses more than1MiB with VALIDATION DETAIL TOO LARGE; it never truncates or substitutes an empty row. Large-row chunking/streaming export remains pending; complete private report data is retained. Values remain in page memory and are cleared on logout. These are historical cut values, not live queries or repair. Repair is separate from read-only validation. The new managed repair workflow requires plan review and explicit confirmation;validation itself never changes destination data.

title: Manual target corrections
text: Manual target corrections 中文 Administrators can add missing rows, correct values and delete extra rows after a destination SQL failure. The first profile covers transactional PostgreSQL and MySQL destinations and uses the existing recovery permissions and pause fence. 1. Pause the whole task and confirm the destination fence. Retain fresh failure evidence. If the original destination commit is ahead of the journal acknowledgment, reconcile it first. 2. Choose “Correct target rows” in the evidence dialog. Select an affected table and action, fill the fields and add the edit to the batch. To import, choose a JSON file or paste the original JSON. 3. Preview the corrections. Review the destination, tables, identities, before and after values and row count. Generate a fresh preview after changing the batch. 4. Enter an approval reason and confirm. Check the operation status and the destination before explicitly resuming the original transaction. Action Input --- --- Insert A keyed table and complete values, including nullable columns and materialized generated columns Update All key fields or an existing ROW ID, plus the fields to change Delete All key fields or an existing ROW ID Each batch supports up to 50 rows and 128 KiB of input. Preview values are limited to 512 KiB. An identity can occur once per batch. JSON string values preserve precision, JSON null represents SQL NULL and JSON columns accept JSON text in a string. Send expectedRevision , subscriptionId , the subscriber's errorCount , correction.evidenceId and correction.evidenceHash to POST /api/tasks/ task /corrections/schema or /corrections/preview . Preview also accepts either correction.batch or original correction.importJson . Submit that same content to the task's /actions endpoint with action: CORRECTION EXECUTE , the preview hash as approvedHash , an approval reason and an X-Request-ID . Retry a lost response with the same request ID and original body. Situation Action --- --- The checkpoint, task revision or target row changed Retain current evidence and preview again A keyless table contains identical values Use the exact ROW ID from normalized evidence A row write or receipt fails Inspect the error and constraints before generating a new preview. The target transaction rolls back the entire batch The table has unsupported foreign keys, triggers or structure Resolve the dependency or use a repair procedure for that table A decimal or integer exceeds browser precision Enter the value as a string before any floating point conversion The administrator preview returns row values. Task summaries and durable receipts expose table scope, counts and the digest. The destination transaction preserves the source log, GTID and acknowledgment position.

title: Messaging targets
text: Messaging targets: configuration, consumption and recovery 中文：消息目标. Example: messaging-v3.yml. Source/journal operations: V3 manual. Implemented scope V3 implements Kafka, RabbitMQ AMQP 0-9-1, NATS JetStream and Redis Streams publishers. Pulsar transport and pipeline wiring are implemented; mixed recovery acceptance passed. Each destination has its own delivery thread, publication/snapshot checkpoint and error generation. They can run alongside MySQL, PostgreSQL and Gauss targets. A stalled destination does not occupy another delivery thread; all subscriptions still govern journal retention. RocketMQ native TCP has a separately accepted initial transport profile below; snapshot/CDC and three mixed broker restart rounds passed. Artemis Core transport and pipeline wiring are implemented; the focused seven-message-product recovery case passed; see the latest evidence below. ActiveMQ Classic remains required work. The contract is confirmed at-least-once publication . The broker and journal database do not share a transaction. Lost confirmations, or a crash between confirmation and receipt persistence, can cause duplicates. Retries retain event IDs and content; consumers must deduplicate durably. A publisher checkpoint means broker confirmation, not completion of downstream business processing or readiness for cutover. Configuration and UI Choose a message product in the V3 wizard, map each source database to a message namespace and add other SQL/message destinations. The UI provides topic/stream, Kafka security/SASL mechanism, Pulsar admin/cluster, RocketMQ prefix/cluster/broker/retention, token, replica count and size limit, masks credentials, and saves a stopped configuration. Import YAML for multiple endpoints or advanced deployment settings. Namespaces start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores, up to 63 characters. url and messaging.endpoints reject embedded credentials and query parameters. Use separate username/password fields or messaging.token for NATS. Passwords/tokens support $ ENV NAME references and are excluded from events/status. Check opens connections and reads capabilities; it creates no business queues, streams or replication connection. Artemis uses a temporary non-durable management reply channel. Destination cards expose only product, mapping, consistency and consumer topic/stream names; connection URLs and credentials are excluded. A broker confirmation and the downstream consumer's business checkpoint are distinct. Setting Meaning --- --- autoCreate Create resources before first publication. False requires pre-provisioning. Previously initialized missing resources are never recreated automatically replicas JetStream/Kafka replicas, Redis total copies (primary included), or the initial quorum queue member count; does not provision broker nodes maxMessageBytes Complete UTF-8 JSON envelope limit, default 1 MiB; broker limits also apply connectTimeoutMillis / requestTimeoutMillis Connection and confirmation/management timeout, 100–120000 ms endpoints Additional entrances to the same broker cluster, never independent replacement clusters Kafka topic Dedicated topic for this subscription; all mapped databases/tables share it Kafka securityProtocol / saslMechanism PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL PLAINTEXT, SASL SSL; SASL supports PLAIN and SCRAM-SHA-256/512 For Rabbit's default / vhost use amqp://host:5672 or amqp://host:5672/%2f . amqp://host:5672/ selects an empty vhost name under the AMQP URI specification. Additional nodes must use the same scheme/vhost. amqps:// and NATS tls:// use JVM trust configuration. Username/password or token authentication is implemented; NKey/JWT files, certificate wizard and a complete TLS acceptance matrix remain pending. Resources and confirmation Each namespace uses namespace. schema , namespace. transactions and namespace.table . Names containing routing syntax, excessive length, or a / rm prefix use rm followed by SHA-256(table ID) for the table channel. The envelope/schema retain the original database/table names. Control channels are reserved. Kafka writes all logical channels into messaging.topic , retaining the channel in the rivomesh channel header. A dedicated single-partition topic is required, with acks=all, enable.idempotence=true and max.in.flight=1. This is not a native transactional Kafka producer; the same at-least-once contract applies. Replicas match configuration, min.insync.replicas is replicas/2+1 , unclean election is disabled, retention.ms/bytes are -1 and cleanup.policy is delete. Plan consumer archival/retention; compaction must not silently evict history. Partition growth or policy changes require a plan. One partition has hardware throughput limits. Every broker must disable auto.create.topics.enable ; explicit first-time Admin creation remains available. Otherwise producer metadata refresh could recreate a deleted empty topic and conceal lost history. Preparation checks every broker and requires the relevant DescribeConfigs permission. Topics need Describe/DescribeConfigs/Write and initially Create. Existing replica/ISR/size/retention mismatches block rather than being overwritten. The stable Kafka clusterId is bound in the journal; reconnecting to another cluster raises BROKER IDENTITY CHANGED . Rabbit uses durable, nonexclusive, non-auto-delete queues, direct routing through the default exchange, persistent messages, publisher confirms and mandatory/return. Returns/nacks never advance the receipt. Quorum is the default; classic is selectable. Created queues use reject-publish overflow. Broker policies must not silently discard old/expired messages or dead-letter redeliveries without a recovery consumer. Production quorum requires multiple nodes and appropriate replicas. Single-node tests do not establish majority-loss or power-loss guarantees. NATS uses JetStream publish ACKs and Nats-Msg-Id , never volatile Core NATS. Streams require File storage, Limits retention, Discard New, no age expiry, exact namespace. subjects and configured replicas. The description binds pipeline/subscription/generation; incompatible existing streams are rejected rather than altered. Finite capacity rejects new publication. The publisher does not automatically delete consumer history: plan capacity, archival and consumer checkpoints. Broker fsync, replication and disk determine power-loss durability. Pre-provisioned streams with autoCreate: false must match the same properties and binding. The binding is rivomesh: plus SHA-256(pipelineId + ':' + subscriptionId + ':' + generation) . Read generation from initialized status; prefer service creation for a new task rather than guessing it. Redis Streams The first Redis profile supports a direct standalone primary running Redis 7.2 or newer . Use redis://host:6379/0 or rediss://host:6379/0 , a database number, separate ACL username/password and messaging.stream . Additional endpoints, Sentinel, Cluster routing and proxy failover are not implemented in this profile. rediss enables hostname verification and JVM trust configuration; actual TLS acceptance remains pending. All logical channels share one physical stream. Each entry contains body , rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , optional rivomesh key , and transport headers. Redis-generated entry IDs are transport positions, not event identities or MySQL order. Consumers use the same envelope staging/deduplication rules as other message targets. The reserved marker consumer group rivomesh stream marker v1 creates an empty stream without a fake business event; it is not a consumer checkpoint. Preparation requires AOF enabled, maxmemory-policy=noeviction , no TTL on either stream or ownership keys, and a writable non-cluster primary. Ownership is bound per stream in rivomesh publication owners v1 . Existing unowned streams require an adoption plan; another binding is rejected. Previously initialized missing resources are not silently recreated. XADD NOMKSTREAM prevents accidental recreation after deletion while connected. Administrators must not purge/trim/expire these keys; same-name replacement or an old storage backup still requires reconciliation. Each batch uses XADD followed by WAITAOF on the same physical connection . Both returned fsync counts must satisfy local =1 and replicas = replicas-1 ; a timeout alone is not confirmation. The socket factory forbids SDK socket reopening: retries construct a new authenticated client with the configured database, preventing accidental writes into database 0. Server run ID and client ID are also compared around publication to reject hidden connection replacement. AOF write failure, insufficient replicas, OOM under noeviction and disconnection preserve the receipt and retry. replicas: 1 confirms only local AOF, without Redis failover durability. Higher counts require the corresponding live replicas with AOF; they do not provision replication or prove lossless promotion. RDB alone and volatile Pub/Sub are insufficient. The publisher ACL needs connection/auth/select as applicable, INFO, CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy, CLIENT ID, EXISTS/TYPE/PTTL, HGET/HSETNX, XGROUP CREATE, XADD and WAITAOF, limited to the selected stream and ownership hash. Consumers need their own read/group permissions. check reads capabilities without creating keys. WAITAOF and fsync can affect latency; measure against the actual storage and replication topology. No automatic stream trimming is performed; capacity and consumer-safe archival remain an operator responsibility. Pulsar Pulsar uses a dedicated persistent, non-partitioned topic for all mapped namespaces. Configure url: pulsar://host:6650 , messaging.adminUrl: http://host:8080 , cluster , and topic: persistent://tenant/namespace/topic . The tenant/namespace must already exist and belong to exactly the configured cluster; geo-replication needs a separate plan. The first profile uses one service endpoint with native broker discovery; extra endpoints and username/password authentication are rejected. Token authentication uses messaging.token . TLS requires both pulsar+ssl:// and HTTPS admin access with hostname verification. Actual token/TLS and multi-broker/BookKeeper-failure acceptance remain pending. Every active broker must disable automatic topic creation and inactive-topic deletion and enable topic-level policies. Namespace overrides must not re-enable automatic creation. The publisher reads these settings through advertised admin endpoints, requiring cluster/broker/namespace management-read permissions as well as topic operations. Native reconnect must not recreate a deleted empty topic. Restrict administrative policy changes during publication; existence/binding checks cannot detect every purge or restoration of an old backup. Initial creation atomically binds rivomesh.owner to the common pipeline/subscription/generation binding and marks rivomesh.provision=BUILDING V1 . Only that unfinished owned topic is provisioned: infinite retention in both time and size, TTL 0, inactive deletion disabled, BookKeeper persistence, and backlog policies that reject producers rather than evict consumers' history. Applied policies are verified before marking READY V1 and opening a producer. Asynchronous policy propagation retries without publishing. Existing READY policy mismatches, unowned topics or another binding require a plan and are not overwritten. Pre-provisioning with autoCreate: false requires matching ownership, READY V1 and all policies; missing initialized topics never get an empty replacement. replicas means minimum BookKeeper ACK copies for this profile. Fresh topics use ensemble/write/ACK quorum all equal to this value. An existing compatible topic may use a larger ensemble/write quorum if its ACK quorum meets the configured minimum. This setting does not provision bookies, broker replicas or failure domains. Confirmations rely on BookKeeper's durable journal/replication configuration and recoverable metadata. A single-bookie test is not a production HA or power-loss guarantee. Retention is infinite, so plan capacity, archival and consumer-safe history removal. Publication sends bytes synchronously with batching/chunking disabled and bounded pending requests. Message properties carry immutable event ID, logical channel and transport headers; the Pulsar key carries the logical row/transaction key. BookKeeper-confirmed send completion precedes the journal receipt. Pulsar message IDs and broker-side deduplication are not substitutes for event-ID deduplication and transaction staging. Native Pulsar transactions are not used; the common at-least-once contract applies across producer replacement and source lease handoff. The Java 8 client is pinned to Pulsar 4.0.14 behind rivomesh-pulsar-transport . Its logging, crypto, Jackson annotations and protobuf are isolated from core dependencies. This is deliberate: later Pulsar client branches require newer Java, while the 4.0 branch retains Java 8 support. Build the reactor with mvn verify so the private SDK is packaged before the application. The transport test runs with the core JAR first on the classpath and verifies both dependency sets coexist; it also verifies read-only check, ownership, send/read, broker restart, retention refusal and lost-topic protection. Full mixed-pipeline recovery acceptance is recorded separately in validation. Broker startup and source catch-up are different measurements. The failure harness first verifies that SQL continues while stopped brokers report automatic retry, then waits for broker health, then measures catch-up without manual Resume. A broker whose admin service or storage is still starting cannot be treated as a ready destination. Recovery diagnostics include safe error codes such as PULSAR ADMIN HTTP 503 ; no row data or credentials are copied into status. Pulsar references: Java baseline decision, topics and resource management, retention versus TTL, broker configuration API. Server storage identity and recovery must be validated for the chosen deployment. Envelope and consumer rules Version 1 includes pipeline/subscriptionId/generation/event ID, kind/namespace, table/schema version, source position and sequence. Publication IDs include subscription identity to prevent deduplication across different mappings; Change.eventId still identifies the logical source event. Values are interpreted through the schema. Numeric strings retain precision; present: false means absent and present: true, value: null means SQL NULL. JSON null is a JSON text value and differs from SQL NULL. Kind Meaning --- --- SCHEMA Columns/types/identity/source indexes; message sinks do not execute DDL/index conversion SNAPSHOT BEGIN , SNAPSHOT ROW , SNAPSHOT END Snapshot ID/baseline/parts/row ordinals/counts; complete only after END and deduplicated counts match BEGIN , ROW , COMMIT Source commit boundary/order/before/after images; COMMIT is published after all row confirmations Primary-key updates expose both beforeKey and afterKey : remove the old identity and insert/update the new identity. Keyless duplicate rows each have a separate rowId. Delete the specified occurrence, not all equal rows. Snapshot and CDC share these occurrence identities. Transaction controls include global totalChanges , per-namespace expectedChanges , transactionKind and source attributes; controls preserve BARRIER changes at their original ordinals. Row ordinals cover the whole transaction projected to that destination. Consumers should durably stage and deduplicate events, await the required rows and COMMIT, verify counts/order, then atomically commit their business work and consumer checkpoint. Different queues/subjects can be consumed at different speeds: an application may observe COMMIT before all rows arrive. COMMIT contentHash is the Codec SHA-256 of the normalized SourceTransaction projected through this destination's mappings. A consumer subscribed to every mapped namespace can reconstruct it from BEGIN's transaction ID/generation/position/kind/attributes and ordered ROW.change values. A consumer of only some namespaces cannot claim to verify the entire hash. Transport epochs are headers outside immutable bodies. Track generation/sequence to prevent late old publications from overwriting newer state; timestamps are not source order. Neither the NATS duplicate window nor Rabbit message IDs replace durable consumer deduplication. Consumer ACKs, crashes, transaction staging capacity, missing rows and long outages require a consumer recovery protocol; this version does not ship an automatically running materialization consumer. Kafka producer idempotence also does not cover all replay after replacing a producer instance. Broker offsets are not source sequences. Handle late old-owner publications through generation/epoch/logical sequence/event ID, not physical offset alone. Consumers selecting one namespace filter envelopes and verify that namespace's expectedChanges. Recovery and FAQ Disconnect/restart: retryable failures preserve checkpoints, reconnect, revalidate established resources and replay unconfirmed work. Permanent permission/routing/property failures pause only that destination. Repair and select its generation-bound Resume action in the UI. Missing queue/stream: MESSAGE DESTINATION MISSING REBUILD REQUIRED requires restoring original broker storage or a recovery plan covering consumers, missing history and a new snapshot. Creating an empty resource and pressing Resume cannot prove historical completeness. An administrator purging/replacing a same-name resource or changing broker policies cannot be detected by an existence check alone; reconcile the data. Cross-target atomicity: destinations confirm independently. One may succeed while another fails. There is no cross-database/broker distributed transaction. Source history remains until lagging subscribers catch up; quota exhaustion stops capture rather than dropping their data. Pause/cutover: message destinations return UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT PUBLICATION . A journal epoch cannot retract a broker request already in flight. Fence/stop old producers, establish downstream catch-up barriers, reconcile and isolate business writes before cutover. Automated cutover remains in development. Oversized messages: MESSAGE TOO LARGE preserves the transaction checkpoint. Align application/broker limits and consumer memory. Transparent fragmentation/external LOB storage is unimplemented. Large source transactions, catalog memory and growing receipt history still require resource work; there is no hardware-independent capacity guarantee. Redis confirmation does not arrive: inspect AOF health, required replica AOF fsyncs, replication lag, disk and ACL. REDIS DURABILITY NOT CONFIRMED or REDIS CONNECTION CHANGED DURING CONFIRM leaves publication unconfirmed and replayable, even if XADD already reached the server. Fix the cause without deleting stream history or weakening a running task's durability configuration. The UI's source snapshot rows are source preparation progress; per-destination snapshot confirmations are separate and still do not prove consumer completion. Verification: run SYNC MAVEN CACHE=/path/to/cache bash tests/messaging-run.sh . It creates/restarts/removes only its own Compose project. See validation for versions, results and remaining cluster/TLS acceptance. Protocol references: Kafka 3.9 Java baseline, producer configuration, Rabbit Java client/Java 8 baseline, Rabbit reliability, NATS Java client, JetStream. Protocol documentation does not substitute for this project's environment acceptance. Redis references: WAITAOF same-connection semantics and returned counts, persistence, Jedis. The current client is Jedis 8.0.2 using its single-connection API. RocketMQ native TCP profile The ROCKETMQ publisher is implemented using Java-8-compatible native client 5.5.1 with isolated dependencies. Real native-broker confirmation, client/broker restart, unsafe flush refusal and lost-topic protection passed ( target/rocketmq-transport-cached.log ); mixed snapshot/CDC, worker kill and three broker restart rounds passed ( target/messaging-rocketmq-mixed.log , 49 executions). Cluster, ACL and TLS support are not claimed. The first profile is a single ASYNC MASTER broker group with one local synchronous disk copy , not a synchronous replicated or Raft guarantee. replicas must be 1; username/password/token are rejected until an authenticated profile is verified. Use a trusted network for this profile. Configure rocketmq://nameserver:9876 , optional additional NameServers in messaging.endpoints , cluster , broker , topic and minimumRetentionHours . The URI is a native TCP NameServer, not a 5.x gRPC Proxy. topic is a prefix of 1–48 characters (letter first, then letters/digits/underscore/hyphen). The physical topic is prefix 64-hex task/subscription/generation binding . The UI exposes that actual name once the journal generation exists. New generations receive different names; restarting the same generation reuses its name. Reserve these names exclusively for Rivomesh and prohibit external creation, deletion, expansion or writes. Preparation reads broker configuration and creates exactly one read/write queue on the selected broker group. The broker must have flushDiskType=SYNC FLUSH , transientStorePoolEnable=false , autoCreateTopicEnable=false , cleanFileForciblyEnable=false , and fileReservedTime = minimumRetentionHours (default 87600 hours). DLedger/controller/replicated profiles are rejected. Deploy these durability settings at broker startup; do not change storage mode live. The client sends persistent synchronous messages with waitStoreMsgOK and accepts only SEND OK ; disk/slave timeout statuses do not advance the journal checkpoint. Retries can duplicate events with the same stable ID. Queue offset 0 contains an ownership manifest identified by user property rivomesh publication manifest . Consumers must filter this manifest before decoding JSON envelopes. Subsequent messages use the common event envelope and rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , rivomesh key properties. All logical tables/control channels share queue 0. Consumers still deduplicate and verify SNAPSHOT END / COMMIT and row counts; native broker confirmation does not mean application completion. The manifest permits a crash between topic creation and publication to finish on restart. A nonempty topic with another manifest, missing initialized topic, changed queue/policy, or expired offset 0 blocks with a recovery error. Each publication batch rechecks broker settings, topic shape and manifest. No automatic empty-history replacement is permitted. Retention is finite : plan downstream archival and a verified rebuild before its horizon; large retention values are not infinite storage. Storage loss, manual cleanup, quota and retention expiry require a recovery plan. Monitor broker disk capacity; do not lower retention to clear pressure silently. Run bash tests/rocketmq-transport-run.sh for the actual release-JAR/broker test. The test uses isolated native broker 5.5.0, no host ports, startup data-volume ownership initialization and removes only its Compose project. The default anonymous single-node test does not validate ACL, TLS, power loss, controller/DLedger, replica failover or sustained throughput. Protocol references: server configuration and native client source. A matching manifest alone does not prove retained confirmed history. RocketMQ now also persists and verifies a native confirmation receipt as described below. Other message transports still need their own rollback-detection profiles; do not infer that this protects every broker product. RocketMQ native confirmation receipts After a successful publication batch, the journal saves a generation-bound native receipt before schema/snapshot/transaction receipts advance. New table publication transport contains one small row per subscription; this additive table is created when opening existing journals. Its update is lease-fenced and compares the previously read receipt, so a stale worker cannot replace a newer receipt. Confirmation loss or an uncertain metadata commit still replays stable IDs. ROCKETMQ OFFSET V1 binds the physical topic, queue offset, CommitLog byte offset and a SHA-256 digest of the stable event ID plus message body. On reconnect and before each publication batch, native viewMessage reads the CommitLog record and verifies that receipt. This avoids treating asynchronous ConsumeQueue indexing lag as lost confirmed data. Missing, replaced or changed confirmed records block that destination with ROCKETMQ CONFIRMED HISTORY REBUILD REQUIRED , before further publication or resource creation. Normal restart resumes against the saved receipt. An existing publication without its required native receipt blocks with PUBLICATION TRANSPORT UPGRADE REQUIRES PLAN ; a new binary does not invent an unsafe baseline for an older task. target/rocketmq-native-progress-restore.log passed the actual release-JAR test: stop broker, copy its nonempty volume after the first confirmation, restart and confirm another event, restore the older volume, verify the first event remains while the second is missing, and reject continuation with the saved later receipt. It also rejects a changed content digest and accepts a matching receipt through client restart. target/messaging-native-progress.log additionally passed 53 executions: the actual release JAR, six message products plus PostgreSQL, worker kill and three all-broker stop/start rounds with native receipt recovery. These checks protect the saved confirmed record; they are not an arbitrary-history checksum or consumer business checkpoint. Keep the ownership/retention/storage requirements, consumer count/order verification and archival plan. Do not delete the transport receipt or force a lower offset to bypass failure. A validated recovery/rebuild plan is required when confirmed history has been lost. Receipt rows and other metadata require physical storage headroom beyond the logical event quota. target/v3-native-progress-external.log passed 47 executions, including the native receipt persistence/CAS/lease/reopen contract against actual MySQL, PostgreSQL and openGauss journal storage, plus V3 SQL fan-out and HTTP controls. target/ui-native-progress.log passed 16 DOM tests. Artemis Core retained-queue profile ACTIVEMQ ARTEMIS is a separate product from ActiveMQ Classic. Configure artemis://host:61616 , username/password, explicit database mappings and messaging.stream as a 1–48-character queue prefix (letter first, then letters/digits/underscore/hyphen). messaging.broker optionally checks the broker name. The first profile accepts one entrance, replicas: 1 and no token/extra endpoints. The physical queue is prefix . 64-hex pipeline/subscription/generation binding ; the UI exposes it after generation initialization. The client speaks Core protocol through isolated rivomesh-artemis-transport . Java 8 compatibility uses Core client 2.19.1 with privately pinned Netty 4.1.130 and separate logging/JSON libraries. Current clients requiring Java 11 are not loaded into a Java 8 worker. Acceptance is against broker 2.57.0, whose runtime is independent of the worker JDK. This is a tested compatibility profile, not a claim that every older client/broker/security configuration is supported. The broker must enable persistence, transactional and nontransactional journal sync; preparation reads these runtime attributes. Keep journal-datasync=true in the broker configuration: the management attributes used here do not independently expose/verify that setting. The supplied broker fixture sets it explicitly and uses NIO. Physical storage durability and power-loss acceptance remain separate requirements. A synchronous Core transaction commit precedes publication receipts; lost confirmations still permit stable-ID duplicates. Use a dedicated address-settings match such as rivomesh. for that prefix. Disable auto-create queues/addresses and all auto-delete variants for business resources; the service explicitly creates its first reserved queue. Disable expiry ( no-expiry=true , or all expiry delays -1), last-value/ring/purge behavior and delivery discard ( max-delivery-attempts=-1 ). PAGE/BLOCK/FAIL address policies are accepted; DROP is rejected. A persistent non-destructive ANYCAST queue with exactly one queue bound to its address is required. Existing incompatible resources are refused. Do not change journal-datasync or these policies underneath a running task. Management travels over the same authenticated Core connection, not a separate HTTP admin URL. It uses a temporary non-durable activemq.management. uuid reply queue. Grant the needed management, temporary-queue create/delete, send/consume/browse rights and allow cleanup for this internal prefix. Check creates no business objects; its temporary control channel closes afterward. Do not apply the business no-create policy to this reply prefix. The example fixture separates these address settings; merge the relevant settings into an existing deployment rather than replacing its entire broker configuration blindly. Queue offset/record ordering is internal to Artemis. A retained ownership message carries rivomesh publication manifest ; consumers filter that property before decoding subsequent bytes as the common JSON envelope. Published properties carry rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , rivomesh key and the common headers. Normal consumer ACK does not delete messages from this non-destructive queue. After reconnect consumers may receive older events again and must use durable deduplication/business checkpoints. Native Core byte consumption is tested; AMQP/JMS consumer variants still need their own interoperability acceptance. The service binds the broker's persistent node ID and queue ID in the journal after preparation. Missing initialized queues, changed incarnations, wrong ownership or unsafe queue shape block before publication receipts advance. Preparation can finish an interrupted empty reserved queue; initialized resources are not replaced. The identity is rechecked around publication. After each confirmed batch, the journal also saves ARTEMIS RECORD V1 with physical queue, native message ID, event ID and a length-prefixed event/body SHA-256. Before resuming or sending another batch, a filtered Core browser checks that exact persistent record and content. Missing/changed history blocks even when a restored older nonempty backup retains the same node/queue IDs. This checks the last saved confirmation, not every earlier record or downstream business checkpoint. Existing publications without a native receipt require an explicit migration/rebuild plan; never clear metadata to continue. An empty initialized replacement is rejected without writing a new ownership message. Why does ACK retain history? This profile intentionally keeps the publication log. Plan disk capacity, consumer archival and an explicit rebuild/retention workflow; normal consumer ACK does not reclaim this queue. Can I use an ordinary destructive queue? No; it fails profile validation. Can I point this at ActiveMQ Classic? No; Classic has a distinct protocol/profile and is not implemented by this adapter. Why did Check fail with permissions? In addition to data access, Core management needs its temporary reply-channel grants. The response does not expose credentials or message contents. target/artemis-transport-volume-fixed.log passed Java 8 client/current-broker publication, exact bytes/key/channel, non-destructive consumer ACK, broker/client restart with stable identities, unsafe queue refusal and missing initialized queue protection. Its first failed log concerned isolated data-volume permissions, not protocol acceptance. target/artemis-wiring-unit.log passed 44 core executions; target/ui-artemis-fixed.log passed 17 DOM cases after fixing a product-switch credential visibility bug. Earlier seven-message-product runs failed (timeouts); the later focused case passed as separately recorded below. Cluster, paging-pressure, TLS, power-loss and broader version/security acceptance remain pending. Management API, persistence, address settings. target/artemis-native-progress-final.log passed against the actual release JAR: snapshot the stopped isolated broker volume after one confirmed record, publish a later record, restore the older nonempty volume, prove node/queue IDs are unchanged, and reject the later receipt. Matching receipts resume; altered digests, malformed receipts and empty replacement queues are rejected. The empty replacement remains empty. target/ui-artemis-native-progress.log passed 17 DOM cases. Seven-product mixed recovery is being rerun separately after a previous run recorded source/HTTP timeouts during host sleep. These results do not prove cluster, TLS, paging pressure or power-loss behavior. Admin retry diagnostics and focused recovery reruns PULSAR ADMIN TIMEOUT means a client-side admin timeout; PULSAR ADMIN CONNECT RETRY means a failed connection. The SDK can wrap either in an exception whose default status is 500, without receiving an HTTP 500 response. Check broker access logs before diagnosing a server error. PULSAR ADMIN REQUEST FAILED preserves an ambiguous generic SDK failure without inventing an HTTP response. Actual HTTP response failures retain their status codes. Credential-provider/TLS rejections are permanent configuration faults; this classification does not constitute TLS interoperability acceptance. Snapshot preparation now emits deduplicated retry diagnostics with exception classes and stack locations, excluding exception messages, credentials, SQL and rows. A transient network fault retains RUNNING and the existing error generation; no manual resume should be needed. Inspect host/VM load, heap/direct memory, broker readiness, network and configured request timeouts rather than assuming a hardware-independent startup/catch-up deadline. After a full build, a focused fault rerun can reuse the accepted release and compiled tests: The checker refuses changed Java sources, stale tests/assets or an invalid release, and verifies the pinned Java-8-compatible JUnit console checksum. This runs one pipeline case , not the full 54-execution Maven suite. Default invocation still builds and runs the wider suite. Failed runs retain full Pulsar logs and bounded other-broker logs under target/broker-tests/ project / ; cleanup affects only that test project. Optional RIVOMESH TEST JAVA OPTIONS supplies JVM diagnostic flags to the isolated test and worker processes, for example -XX:+PrintGCDetails -XX:+PrintGCTimeStamps on Java 8. It is a test setting, not a production sizing recommendation. Latest focused acceptance target/messaging-pulsar-gc-diagnostics.log : one real pipeline case passed, zero failed/skipped , on the actual Java 8 release JAR (256 MiB worker heap). PostgreSQL plus Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS/Redis/Pulsar/RocketMQ/Artemis complete snapshot/CDC, worker kill and three all-message-broker stop/start rounds; SQL continues during broker outage, retry diagnostics persist and clear automatically after catch-up. Finally deleting Artemis's initialized queue pauses only that target while all other subscriptions catch up. Native receipts restore through restart. This took about 590 seconds on the busy shared host, with Java 8 GC diagnostics enabled; no heap/deadline increase was used. It is one focused case, not a fresh pass of the entire 54-execution Maven suite, nor a general capacity/recovery-time promise.

title: Node registry
text: Shared node registry and heartbeat For current deployment, see the multi-node guide. Accounts, sessions and audit can now be shared by explicitly enabling shared access. Registry-only installations keep them local. Task operations are local by default. Optional fixed-owner global control is integrated; explicit controller/Agent separation has initial acceptance, while automatic relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. 中文：节点目录. Contract: CP-01. This feature shares node observations. Accounts, sessions and audit can be shared by explicitly enabling shared access; task/configuration operations are local by default. Optional fixed-owner global control is integrated; explicit controller/Agent separation has initial acceptance, while automatic relocation and additional failover profiles remain open. ADMIN opens Node registry . Standalone mode shows one node with an ID retained in private node-id . With a shared control database, all endpoints in the same clusterId read the same directory. VIEWER/OPERATOR retain existing task grants without global registry access. Cards show release SHA/version, real JVM/architecture/CPU/heap, configured task/running capacities, registration epoch, database observation time, heartbeat/expiry and task IDs/Worker state/observation time. HEALTHY means a valid heartbeat lease, not healthy data destinations. STALE means expiry; STOPPED means graceful deregistration committed. Query failure clears old healthy cards instead of presenting cached success. Task lists are observations, not global configuration/scheduling authority. Task pages/actions are local by default; optional fixed-owner routing is described in global control. Do not copy/start configurations elsewhere merely because a node is STALE. CDC/target leases still govern execution; registry leases cannot authorize Worker takeover. Shared access, global commands and explicit separated execution have distinct profiles; see global control and execution lifecycle for current acceptance. Linux and Docker Use independent local control, task and report directories and unique stable nodeIds. Sharing controller.json/audit H2 directories or a PVC is not a shared control protocol. See platform-cluster.yml. Initial native control-store profiles are PostgreSQL17 and MySQL8.4. H2 memory is for in-process protocol tests. For MySQL use com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver , a MySQL URL and a database namespace. Tables require InnoDB/utf8mb4 bin; incompatible existing tables are rejected. Configure TLS through driver parameters; production TLS is not disabled automatically. Startup needs schema/database and control-table creation permissions plus SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and bootstrap session-lock access. Existing tables are never cleared/dropped; incompatible formats refuse startup. A shared SQL instance is possible with a separate namespace and dedicated privileges. nodeId, username/password and optional advertiseUrl support a whole-value $ ENV NAME reference. advertiseUrl is observational only, with no user info/path/query/fragment. Connection/query timeouts are bounded; directory APIs omit database URLs, credentials, paths and raw business data. heartbeatMillis is100–30000ms. leaseMillis is1000–300000ms and at least three heartbeat intervals. maximumNodes is1–10000. Defaults are2s/15s/1000. Lease/capacity are consistent cluster settings without online editing. Capacity includes retained STALE/STOPPED records; historical-node administration remains future work. Each node publishes up to200task observations. Keyset pages default to20nodes and allow at most50. Helm and native Kubernetes Set the real URL and an existing username/password Secret in values-cluster.yaml. Install independent releases/PVCs: Each release stays a single-replica Recreate deployment with a stable release-name nodeId. Increasing one Deployment's replicas while sharing its PVC is invalid. Registry-only accounts/sessions remain local. Enable shared access for shared identity/session continuity; this does not provide controller HA. For manual YAML edit/apply node-a and node-b, including image/store/Secret references. Static parity is checked; live Kubernetes/CSI/upgrades/controller HA remain unaccepted. See session HTTPS configuration. Failure handling and FAQ - NODE ID IN USE: another live incarnation holds this ID. Stop the duplicate or use a unique stable ID. After confirmed power loss, wait for expiry without editing epochs. - NODE REGISTRATION FENCED: a replacement owns the registration. The old process cannot renew or deregister it. Correct deployment IDs and restart; this does not establish Worker takeover. - CONTROL STORE PROTOCOL MISMATCH: cluster format/lease/capacity differ or authority metadata is missing. Restore consistent settings/state; startup never overwrites it automatically. - CONTROL STORE UNAVAILABLE / readiness503: registry connection/query failure or expired heartbeat. healthz remains live; Workers follow their own journal leases. After recovery, an expired but unreplaced incarnation re-registers with a higher epoch; replaced processes remain fenced. - Killed nodes briefly remain HEALTHY: until expiry, death cannot be confirmed. Use heartbeat/expiry timestamps; the observation window is not failover authorization. - Old process overwrites replacement: active-ID and incarnation/epoch checks reject old heartbeats and shutdowns. - Graceful shutdown did not show STOPPED: kill, storage failure or lost commit confirmation falls back to STALE through expiry. - Backup/restore: back up the SQL control namespace and each node's existing accounts/audit/configuration/reports. Restoring the registry alone does not restore tasks or provide HA. Rollback of metadata/epochs requires review; external immutable backup anchors remain unfinished. Docker deployment uses http://127.0.0.1:18088 and http://localhost:18089 for two endpoints reading one registry. Different hostnames avoid same-name cookies overwriting across ports. Existing private preview credentials remain; sign in separately. Acceptance fixtures are removed; the development preview remains available.

title: OceanBase
text: OceanBase destination and FAQ 中文：OceanBase V3. Example: oceanbase-v3.yml. Current scope V3 configuration, CLI, fan-out workers and the bilingual wizard are implemented. Native OceanBase CE 4.3.5.6 ARM64/Java 8 transactions, cross-database rollback, ownership/epoch fences, snapshots/types and partial CDC passed. Full mixed restart/recovery acceptance has not passed; the adapter remains EXPERIMENTAL. See the evidence. This does not claim all versions, clusters or Oracle-mode support. product: OCEANBASE uses MySQL Connector/J 8.4.0 and jdbc:mysql:// , normally port 2881. Connect to a MySQL-mode user tenant , usually with rivomesh@business , rather than root@sys . Every new connection verifies OceanBase identity, mode and a non-system tenant, then forces ob read consistency=STRONG . A MySQL wire version is not the OceanBase product version. Oracle mode, seekdb and other compatible products are outside this verified profile. Start and recover Fill in source candidates, the user tenant and explicit database mappings, then supply MYSQL PASSWORD and OCEANBASE PASSWORD . Source GTID/ROW/FULL and privileges are documented in the V3 manual; UI steps are in the console manual. In another terminal use status config/oceanbase-v3.yml . After repairing a deterministic failure, resume the affected target in the UI, or use resume config/oceanbase-v3.yml oceanbase-business 7 with the same java -jar ... prefix. Replace 7 with the current errorGeneration from status; never guess it. Resume retries the original transaction. OceanBase is V3-only; select it in the wizard and provide a user-tenant identity. Extra destinations can select PostgreSQL or other products independently. Data, transactions and indexes Explicit mappings send each source database to a destination database in the same tenant. A configuration can fan out to OceanBase, PostgreSQL and other targets with independent acknowledgements and pauses. Rivomesh can create mapped databases/tables; it does not provision clusters, pools, tenants or users. Business changes and the sink checkpoint commit in one destination transaction, with a metadata row lock and epoch fencing. An uncertain commit is resolved by rereading the sink checkpoint. Capture progress never substitutes for apply progress. Independent destinations do not share a global atomic commit. Keyless tables gain rivomesh row id to retain duplicate multiplicity; business users must not edit it. UINT64 uses DECIMAL(20,0), decimals keep declared precision, JSON uses native JSON, binary uses LONGBLOB, and temporal values follow the relational-target mappings. Supported source generated expressions are evaluated by the existing source adapter and their values are copied into ordinary target columns. Procedures, triggers, foreign keys, partition layouts, physical index distribution and generated expressions are not automatically reproduced. Existing incompatible targets require an adoption plan. The default uniquePolicy: DOWNGRADE BUSINESS converts business UNIQUE indexes into ordinary indexes. Primary/actual identity keys must remain unique. Plain BTREE/simple GSI can use the current ordinary-index plan; global routing, global uniqueness and source partition semantics are not preserved. Expressions, prefixes, descending keys, fulltext and spatial methods require an explicit plan. PRESERVE can retain representable business uniqueness, subject to native DDL constraints; it does not reproduce arbitrary GSI semantics. Downgrading assumes exclusive synchronization writes, valid source constraints and complete ordered source transactions. It does not guarantee uniqueness under independent target writes. Existing UNIQUE constraints are never silently dropped. Before takeover, stop incremental writes, reconcile the data and restore required constraints. The complete automated takeover workflow remains pending. Deployment and privileges Use the same V3 task document with Linux, Docker, Helm or native Kubernetes deployment. Rivomesh manifests do not deploy OceanBase itself; database operations manage production clusters, OBProxy, tenant resources and isolation. The target account needs metadata access and appropriate mapped-database/table/index creation and business/metadata read/write privileges. A successful connection check does not prove all DDL/DML privileges. Supply passwords through environment references or protected configuration. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery. Cross-host worker takeover uses the already-supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journal. journal.product: OCEANBASE is rejected until that backend has its own acceptance. Controller HA and live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance remain separate work. Failures and FAQ - Tenant mismatch: verify the user suffix, OBProxy routing and tenant compatibility mode. System/Oracle tenants are rejected; mode is never changed automatically. - Outage/restart: recognized transient connection failures back off and reconnect, then catch up from destination progress. Other sinks continue until journal backpressure applies. OceanBase manages its own leader elections; multi-node/OBProxy failover needs separate acceptance. - SQL failure: only the affected subscription pauses. Repair permissions, types or constraints, then use the current errorGeneration in UI/CLI to replay the original transaction. Restart does not bypass the pause or skip events. - Deleted tables/metadata: an empty replacement is not silently created under an old checkpoint. Preserve evidence and plan a rebuild. A normal resume cannot repair deleted data or lost history. - Why STRONG reads: a recovery decision must observe committed checkpoint state. WEAK reads can return an older value; URL settings cannot override this profile's STRONG requirement. - Why a separate product from MYSQL: the wire protocol is similar, but vendor, tenant and consistency requirements differ. - Source DDL: initial auto-creation does not imply complete online DDL. Unsupported structural changes retain safe progress and require a conversion plan; do not edit GTIDs to bypass them. Full DDL, reconciliation/repair and migration workflows remain pending. - Existing targets: compatible empty tables can pass shape/ownership checks. A newly adopted nonempty table needs a provable baseline and adoption plan even if it looks identical. Rivomesh does not silently clear it or attach an unproved checkpoint. - Capacity: fixture CPU/memory/disk quotas are correctness-test settings, not hardware throughput standards. Benchmark row width, transaction size, indexes, fan-out, backlog windows and tenant resources. Hardware capacity reports remain pending. Official references - Official Docker fixture and resource settings - MySQL-mode transaction control - System variables Test-image startup diagnostics The official all-in-one image is a fixture, not a production deployment. The current fixture sets instance memory limit=5G/system memory=1G, user resource-unit memory size=2G/log disk size=2G, instance logs5G/data2G, and a container limit of 6G/6 CPUs. These are test settings, not production capacity recommendations or throughput standards. Unit memory is not exclusively business-tenant memory: an actual 2GiB unit probe showed roughly 1GiB for the user tenant after splitting with its metadata tenant. Other tenants, caches and host load affect recovery. A boot success! banner is insufficient; this image can print it even when OBD memory checks prevented observer startup. Check the actual observer process, user-tenant connection, container health and OBD logs together. Do not delete existing data or skip synchronization checkpoints to repair inadequate startup resources. Do not blindly use obd cluster start -f ; this version's -f means force-delete, not bypassing resource checks. Recovery acceptance still pending All four mixed runs retain their failures. The first15s administrative-DDL timeout followed successful outage catch-up, worker kill and PostgreSQL constraint isolation. With revised timeouts/catalog checks, the 5GiB instance/2GiB unit remained in user-tenant initialization beyond the recovery deadline; increasing CPU did not make the full case pass. A probe showed roughly 1GiB for the user tenant, which alone does not establish root cause. The6GiB instance/3GiB unit was rejected by OBD's available-memory precheck and never launched observer, despite a success banner. Checks were not bypassed, transactions were not skipped and checkpoints were not reset. These results do not establish complete automatic recovery or attribute every failure to Rivomesh or OceanBase; investigation and full acceptance remain required.

title: Performance & runtimes
text: Performance measurement and hardware reference 中文：性能测量. Hardware capacity must come from reproducible measurements of a stated workload. No rows/second or recovery-time promise applies independently of CPU, memory, storage latency, network, row width, transaction size, table count, target count, indexes, journal mode and competing workloads. Reproduce the first baseline Build the release before starting the benchmark. Do not rebuild that JAR during a run. Python 3, Docker Compose and the three fixture images are required. On macOS, prefix the Python command with caffeinate -i to prevent idle system sleep; lid closure, manual sleep and other suspension still invalidate timing. For a specified resource envelope: The CPU and database-memory limits apply to each database container; the CPU limit also applies to the worker. Default limits are one CPU and 1 GiB per container, with a 256 MiB Java worker heap and 256 MiB database buffers. They are limits, not reserved or dedicated host resources. Results identify actual image IDs, Docker VM CPU/RAM, container limits, database durability settings, JVM version, workload and release SHA-256. The local journal uses a host bind mount; database files use fixture volumes. Record their physical storage separately. Every run uses a random Compose project and copies the release to target/benchmarks/ run-id /app.jar . It creates only its own source/target, ports remain internal, and cleanup removes only that project's containers/volumes. The copied release, private fixture configuration, bounded logs and report.json remain for review. Failed runs produce status: FAILED ; they must not become capacity reference rows. Inspect containers.log for startup/runtime failures. What the measurements mean Field Meaning --- --- snapshotVisibilitySeconds Worker startup through visibility of all initially loaded target rows; includes JVM startup, discovery and automatic target creation snapshotRowsPerSecond Initial row count divided by that visibility interval sourceMutationSeconds Time to commit updates, deletes and inserts at the source cdcCatchUpSeconds First source mutation through visibility of the final target state; includes source writes cdcChangesPerSecond Number of changed rows, including deleted and inserted rows, divided by that interval afterWritesCatchUpSeconds Observed time between finishing source writes and observing the final target state snapshotContentSha256 , cdcContentSha256 Source and target ordered row streams must match, including IDs, versions and exact payload bytes Transactions are bounded to at most 500 changed rows. Validation streams row bytes rather than collecting the dataset in Python memory. Byte validation runs after each timed phase; a count-only match cannot produce a passing report. The final target contains updated rows, the expected deletes and newly inserted rows. Polling and Docker CLI overhead are included in observation times. This profile is one MySQL 8.4 source, one PostgreSQL 17.12 target, one primary-key table, fixed-width ASCII payload and a LOCAL journal. Source loading warms caches; it is not a cold-storage experiment. It measures neither peak sink throughput nor p95/p99 event latency, durable snapshot-END acknowledgement, failover RTO or steady-state saturation. It does not establish JSON/keyless/large-catalog, multi-target, external-journal, commercial database or cluster performance. Building the hardware standard Keep raw reports and run at least three repetitions for every workload/resource combination. Report medians and ranges; compare identical artifacts, versions, durability, dataset and storage. Record idle and loaded host conditions, disk latency/IOPS, network RTT/bandwidth, utilization and sustained backlog growth. Do not extrapolate linearly from CPU quotas or this small local profile. The final reference matrix still needs independent physical-host runs, remote targets, row-width/transaction/table-count sweeps, all targets and both journal modes, sustained soak, consumer backpressure, capacity exhaustion and recovery under backlog. An individual passing smoke run is evidence that this harness works for that dataset, not completion of that matrix. Harness validation scope Small snapshot/CDC checks and a five-JDK/two-journal matrix previously passed;bounded provenance is consolidated in the verification baseline. Duplicate old-candidate reports are removed. These historical results do not certify the current candidate,every connector or a hardware capacity standard. Runtime and journal profiles --java 8 11 17 21 25 selects the corresponding Temurin JRE worker image; default is 8. --journal-mode LOCAL EXTERNAL defaults to LOCAL. The EXTERNAL profile uses a separate journal schema on the same PostgreSQL instance as the target, so journal and sink compete for that container's resources. It is not a remote dedicated journal benchmark. For example: Selecting a runtime is not a compatibility claim. Inspect a passing raw report and actual JVM version. This SQL profile can establish only MySQL-source/PostgreSQL-target snapshot/CDC coverage on that runtime; messaging/security/failover and other drivers need separate runtime acceptance. To run every listed JRE against both journals sequentially, using one unchanged release: The matrix retains progress and per-profile logs in target/runtime-matrix/ id /matrix.json , links each raw benchmark report, and continues independent profiles after a failed profile. A passing profile requires source/target byte checks, observed journal backend, successful cleanup, the expected actual JVM version and the same release SHA-256. Changing the release aborts the matrix. These remain small SQL runtime checks; they do not validate every adapter on every JRE. Do not run other integration suites or rebuild concurrently.

title: Multi-database pipelines
text: multi-database, multi-target pipelines This manual covers multi-database, multi-target synchronization. formatVersion: 3 (V3 in some console labels) identifies the task configuration format, not a database version or development phase. Keep the default for new tasks; changing the number does not migrate an existing task. 中文：V3 运行手册. Updated 2026-11-15. V3 runs through the CLI and Web console. The wizard defaults to v3 and retains v2 single-database tasks. Formats/metadata are isolated; automatic v2 state migration is not implemented. Web wizard and recovery After signing in, create a task: 1. Keep V3 selected, enter the logical source, comma-separated databases, replication serverId and credentials. 2. Map each database explicitly. Add target instances with distinct IDs and their mappings. Select local or external transactional journals and quota. The plan masks every password, including JDBC URL passwords. Saving leaves the task stopped; check before starting. 3. Inspect snapshot/backlog and each subscriber's ACK. “Resume this target” uses its own error generation; global “Resume after repair” uses the pipeline generation. They are distinct operations. 4. Local stop only stops this worker. Shared pause blocks standby claims and attempts target-local fence confirmation. Unreachable targets remain unconfirmed, not falsely declared settled. Global resume does not clear independent target SQL pauses. Web local journals use the controller's private journals/ pipelineId directory. New YAML omits journal.path ; imports selecting an existing CLI journal path are rejected until a journal/target migration plan is prepared. Do not delete old state to bypass this check. External journals can be imported directly. Controller restart retains task/pause intent and the same managed journal/checkpoints. VIEWER/OPERATOR/ADMIN,local accounts/token rotation,exact task grants,configuration editing/history restore and durable audit are implemented. Managed validation and report-driven repair have explicit accepted profiles. Transactional PostgreSQL and MySQL have scoped profiles for commit confirmation, transaction skipping, gap verification, compensation and manual correction. Configure the corresponding gates in the first-release baseline. Plan business cutover separately. See failed transactions for phase diagnostics and recovery boundaries. DOM and real HTTP/database controls passed;visual and live Kubernetes UI acceptance remain pending. Configure and start Use pipeline-v3.yml. List databases within one logical MySQL topology in databases . Each target explicitly maps source databases to destination schemas/databases with mappings . Targets may subscribe to different subsets; every source database needs at least one target. Transactional products include GAUSS , POSTGRESQL , and MYSQL , plus first experimental KINGBASE, DM and OCEANBASE profiles within their documented acceptance boundaries; KAFKA / RABBITMQ / NATS JETSTREAM / REDIS STREAMS / PULSAR use the messaging protocol and map to message namespaces. Each target owns a delivery thread so stalled I/O cannot block others. MySQL journal/targets must be separate physical instances from the source: server uuid checks reject feedback loops even through address aliases. check reads source objects and target connections without initializing state or creating tables. It does not establish all DDL/snapshot privileges. Running creates metadata and missing business tables. Existing tables must match, be empty, and have no foreign keys/triggers. Nonempty targets require a migration plan and are blocked without clearing data. The synchronizer exclusively writes subscribed business tables. Sources require GTID, ROW/FULL, replica-update logging, no transaction compression/partial JSON images, and no anonymous/tagged GTIDs. Snapshots additionally need permission for short FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK : establish the InnoDB read view, verify schema, record GTIDs and open the cursor before releasing the lock. Reading a large table retains its MVCC view and metadata lock; monitor source undo history and waiting DDL. Snapshot, CDC and recovery The UI separates source snapshot preparation from destination delivery. TARGET SNAPSHOT remains active until every subscription has confirmed the current source manifests. “Source snapshot rows” counts source artifacts; each target has its own confirmed-table count. A message confirmation is still not consumer completion. Each completed target table is acknowledged immediately, allowing its source parts to be reclaimed once all targets confirm that table. Source commits and capture positions are journaled atomically. Each table has an independent snapshot baseline and checksummed parts. Completed artifacts are reusable; an incomplete source snapshot restarts the whole table because a lost MVCC read view cannot resume. Target part checkpoints resume committed parts without duplicates. Keyless tables preserve every duplicate occurrence using rivomesh row id ; source columns conflicting with this name are rejected. Complete before images match one occurrence. Identity mutations and normalized events commit once in source order, and every target reuses that result. Slow replay never mutates identities again. JSON comparison ignores object order/numeric scale while preserving SQL NULL versus JSON null. Stored generated values come from the log. Whitelisted deterministic virtual expressions use versioned expressions and historical logged inputs, never current source rows. Destination columns are ordinary materialized columns. Evaluation pins the snapshot SQL mode and UTC. Unlisted functions, missing base images, or historical schema mismatches stop progress. This does not promise arbitrary client-session SQL-mode query semantics. Plan native generated columns and application writes before takeover. Each transactional target commits data and its checkpoint together under an epoch fence. Targets acknowledge independently; one paused target does not stop others. An uncertain commit is resolved by checking the destination transaction ID/content hash before acknowledging the journal. Multiple targets are not one distributed atomic transaction. Table snapshots can have different baselines; cross-table takeover requires a common catch-up point. The MySQL+transactional-SQL common-cut Java service passed initial native acceptance; see Reconciliation foundation. See managed validation and reviewed repair for the initial SQL profiles. Business cutover remains open. Retention follows the slowest subscriber, including paused ones. Snapshot parts are reclaimed only after every target confirms completion; manifests, baselines and keyless identities remain. Losing target metadata after artifact reclamation requires a rebuild plan. maxBytes covers logical event, normalized event, snapshot and identity payloads, including unconsumed normalization workspace reservations. Database indexes, WAL, metadata and free pages need additional capacity; reclamation does not immediately shrink physical files. Large-catalog pagination, physical headroom alerts, receipt compaction and oversized-transaction staging remain unfinished. Logical quotas are not total disk quotas. Raw capture reserves its normalization copy, keyless row IDs and potential identity additions. Normalization consumes that reservation atomically, preventing raw backlog from using the space needed to drain itself. When a slow destination exhausts available capacity, capture waits without advancing unpersisted GTIDs; deliveries, GC and lease heartbeats continue. Recovering consumers free space and capture resumes automatically. Local backpressure does not trigger the source-idle watchdog. Close/pause cancels the blocked receiver before waiting for the dump connection to finish. If one transaction and workspace exceed the entire quota, TRANSACTION EXCEEDS JOURNAL QUOTA preserves the old position.
